Scooters India Limited  
 
18. The Committee was apprised of the pathetic condition of Scooters India Ltd. 
which was the pride of the country in the area of manufacturing of two and three 
wheelers. The Scooters India Limited was incorporated in the year 1972 and was 
inaugurated by the Late Prime Minister, Smt. Indira Gandhi in April, 1973 at Lucknow.  
The production had started from 1975 by the company by making two wheelers at the 
initial stages with the brand name Vijai Super.  It was referred to BIFR in 1992 and BIFR 
sanctioned revival package in 1996.  The two wheelers production was stopped in 1997 
and company was manufacturing three wheeler in place of that.  The Company is 
presently facing a tough competition from companies like Piaggio and Mahindra and 
Mahindra.     The Committee  was informed that the reason behind the sickness of this 
unit is that SIL have set up the plant with obsolete second hand machinery which is 15 to 
20 years old so the scooters made by it face a lot of breakdown problems and Department 
of Heavy Industry has put it under sick unit.  The Committee is surprised to know that 
despite of its serious concern for the revival of Scooters India Ltd., the Department 
has made the provision of Budgetary support to this company to the tune of only 
Rs.4 crore which Commit tee feels is very meagre amount for its revival.  Committee,  
therefore, recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry should make 
adequate Budgetary support for this company at the time of RE stage and at the 
same time, should seriously pursue its 70 c rore rupee project proposal for revival 
through joint venture.  In fact, this important PSE has to diversify its activities 
because it is manufacturing three wheelers which are being phased out in various 
parts of the Country. Mini four wheelers for transp orting goods have fairly good 
market and with the help of Government this PSE may examine the diversification 
issue in right earnest.  
 


Capital Goods Sector  
 
19. Capital Goods Sector is the mother of all manufacturing Industry and is of 
strategic importance  to the national security and economic independence.  The 
Committee was informed that the Capital Goods Sector was on an upswing since March 
2002, due to investments having taken place in the infrastructure, oil & gas sector, power 
sector, steel plants, au tomobile industries etc.  The Capital Goods industry has evolved 
over these years in terms of competitiveness by consolidating.  Hence the number of 
players is few.  Due to its strategic importance for the country, it is essential to encourage 
manufacturing of capital goods rather than import and enhance the value addition and 
technology transfer. The XIth plan period foresees a 9% GDP growth, which would mean 
that the manufacturing industry should grow at least @12% per annum and the capital 
goods sector w hich is at the core of the manufacturing sector should grow at the rate of 
around 18%.   
20. The Committee notes that like for textile industry, the textile machinery forms the 
Capital Goods Sector and for the engineering industry, the machinery forms the capital 
goods sector so unless the capital goods sector develops, the manufacturing sector can not 
develop.  The Committee has been informed by Secretary DHI and other representatives 
during the course of discussion that in the textile machinery sector, th e industry is forced 
to import the automatic looms from China, which are second hand looms.  These looms 
are being dumped from China in India because our looms production has not come up 
with the latest technology.  Although Ministry are putting some restr ictions saying that 
the looms which are being imported should have a useful life left of 10 years, but with 
this certification, it is very difficult to assess the condition of the machinery.  The same 
thing is happening in the machine tools sector of the c ountry where second hand machine 
tools are being imported from Germany and Japan. The Committee feels that such 
imported machines/plants although imported at the lower cost but importers have 
to pay high prices for their maintenance contracts and spares.  The Committee notes 
that the DHI has raised such issue in the development council meeting.   The 
Committee recommends that suitable remedial measures be taken by imposing high 
import duty   and anti dumping duty on second hand machinery in consultation 
with Ministry of Commerce to grow our capital goods Industry.  The Committee 


impresses upon the Government to allocate sufficient fund for the engineering 
industry and R & D activities to sustain the Industrial growth in coming years.  
 
21. The Committee finds that one of the important constraints to the growth of Indian 
Capital Goods Sector is lack of good infrastructure.  Most of the industries especially in 
machine tools, textile machinery and Heavy Electrical equipment segment, are 
fragmented in nature. Ve ndors to these segments have issues related to timely delivery, 
standardization of process, cost, quality, instrument etc. which in turn affects the growth 
of the overall sector.  In order to overcome such  shortcomings, sector specific cluster or 
parks could be set up at suitable locations.   The Committee feels that the Department 
of Heavy Industry needs to provide a road map to establish these clusters and 
provide adequate funds to create facilities for these clusters.  
 
22. The Capital Goods Sector in gen eral and especially the segments like machine 
tools, textiles machinery, heavy electrical equipment etc do not have major R&D, testing 
and other common infrastructure facilities.  Lack of such facilities has been adversely 
affecting the competitiveness of the industry.   The Committee feels that the DHI 
should facilitate such common facility centers in Public Private Participation (PPP) 
mode.  Some of the Common facilities that can be provided are: -  
Common Foundry (for Machine Tool Industry);  
Common Heat T reatment facility (for Machine Tool Industry);  
Accredited Testing Laboratories;  
Design Centre; and  
Centers of Excellence  
 The Committee suggests that PPP based approach could be adopted for this 
purpose, under which group of entrepreneurs or industry asso ciations would be 
encouraged. 
 
23. The Department of Heavy Industries should also assess the logistics requirements 
of the Capital Goods Sector in areas like railways, roads, bridges, etc and ensure that 
infrastructure is developed to meet the needs of tra nsporting heavy individual 
consignments (upto approximately 500 tons) from manufacturing plant/part to the remote 


locations in the country (as in the case of Hindustan Paper Corporation at Cachar Paper 
Mill in North Eastern region) where power stations wou ld be situated.  The Committee 
suggests that DHI should initiate action in this regard in coordination with Ministry 
of Railways, Road Transport & Highways and Ministry of Power etc.  
  
Paper Industry      
24. The Committee was informed that the paper indus try in the country is facing 
problems mainly   because import of newsprint has been permitted without levy of any 
duty as a result imported newsprint is considerably cheaper in the domestic market than 
indigenous newsprint.  Further, the recession in the p aper market has resulted in decrease 
in sale price of paper.  The Committee was further informed that the combined 
performance of Hindustan Paper Corporation Ltd (HPC) and Hindustan Newsprint Ltd. 
(HNL) during the last five years is gradually decreasing due to increase in specific cost of 
productions with adverse inbound logistic, scanty supply of bamboo at Cachar Paper Mill 
and non availability of railway rakes on the MG section linking Cachar Paper Mill to BG 
section.   The Committee also finds that there  is only a token provision of Rs. 0.02 crore. 
towards budgetary support in respect of HPC during BE 2010 -2011 and Rs. 364.31 crore  
is made through I.E.B.R.  The Committee wonders how a huge amount of Rs. 364. 31. 
crore would be generated through I.E.B.R.   The Secretary, DHI informed the 
Committee that implementation of project at Jagdishpur paper mill is yet to be started 
because of non availability of approx 500 acre of land and out of which 250 area is 
required for the plant and rest for the township.  The Committee is of the view that the 
issue regarding   import duty should be discussed in details with the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry, Ministry of Finance and Information and Broadcasting 
before a decision is taken.  The Committee at the same time r ecommends that some 
measures need to be taken to protect the paper industry in the country.  The 
Committee also recommends that the issue regarding supply of Railway rakes on 
the M.G. Section linking Cachar Paper Mills to B.G. Section may be taken up with 
the Ministry of Railways so that speedy completion of conversion of meter gauge  
can be made to help the paper industry in the North -Eastern region.  
 
HMT  


 25. Hindustan Machine Tools is one of the major industry in the country. There are 
three major manufacturing activities covered by HMT (i) watches (ii) machine tools and 
(iii) tractors.  The Committee was informed that there is already a rehabilitation plan for 
HMT holding company and this rehabilitation package is at the advance stage of 
approval.  The  Committee was also informed that HMT machine tools division is doing 
very badly along with its watches division. The poor performance of these units is 
because the HMT have not upgraded the technology for satisfying the emission norms 
and the skilled manp ower have left the company.  HMT bearing is also not doing well 
and HMT International is marginally making profits.  The Committee expresses its 
serious concern over the state of affairs of HMT Ltd. Despite Governments grant of 
two revival packages in the recent past and part of the revival package is still under 
implementation. Despite these revival packages there is no turn around of the units. 
Department of Heavy Industry is contemplating for a Joint Venture and the 
Committee is of the opinion that serio us attempts should be made for the revival of 
HMT Ltd. through the Joint Venture route as a last resort otherwise how long the 
public money can be pumped and drained in keeping the PSE alive. In that 
eventuality some other options including closure have to  be given a serious thought.   
The Committee, therefore, is of the view that necessary budgetary support should be 
given for the upgradation of technology to HMT Ltd. during supplementary 
demands 2010 -2011.  The Government should at the same time also impre ss upon 
bulk buyers in the Government Sector, such as Railways, Indian Airlines, 
Commonwealth Games Organization Committee etc.  to opt, wherever  feasible, for 
HMT products so that this once much achieved and prestigious unit would come out 
of the red.  
  
BHEL 
 
26. The Committee finds that for the BE 2010 -2011 no budgetary support has been 
made for BHEL. However, there is decrease in IEBR in respect of this company for BE 
2010-11. The Committee was informed that BHEL is doing well and it had a turnover of 
Rs. 28,033 crore last year which is an all time high turnover of BHEL. It is trying to re -
enter in to the wind energy sector. BHEL has decided to expand its capacity up to 20,000 


MW by 2011. Bharat Heavy Plate and Vessels (BHPV) has been taken over by the 
company and BHEL are outsourcing a number of things from Richardosn & Crudddas. 
The Committee has made its serious concern on its long waiting list for 
establishment of power plants in the country. Committee finds that it has a pending 
list for customers w ho are waiting for 2 -3 years.  During the discussion with 
representatives of BHEL, Committee has come to know that the main reason for such a 
long waiting list is due to its dependence on outside agencies for material inputs for 
castings, forgings, CRGO Ste el, other material etc. On the other hand BHEL is facing a 
problem of non-availability of skilled manpower like qualified boilers operators, welders, 
electricians, fitters at its various sites and problem with respect to standard turbines and 
boilers. The company is also facing a tough competition from L & T, MHI, Bharat Forge 
– Alstom, BGR and Geo Engineering. The Committee is of the view that fierce 
competition to BHEL from these companies is healthy kind of thing which improves 
the performance of BHEL da y by day. The Committee at the same time feels that 
Capital Goods Industry faces dearth of skilled and trained manpower both at shop 
floor level, as well as managerial level. With growing demand and growth of Capital 
Goods Industry it needs to be provided with adequate skilled manpower. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that DHI should consider providing the 
Industry with assistance for development of skills to employees of PSUs through 
approved training institutes.  For this purpose exclusive Industrial  Training 
Institutes may be established for BHEL or arrangements may be made with various 
ITIs to train batches of students in these vocations for BHEL. The Committee finds 
that no budgetary support has been provided to engineering sector and there is huge  
demand of secondary level engineers in the Capital Goods Sector. The Committee 
therefore recommends that BHEL themselves, meet various engineering clusters 
and support it through various up gradation schemes. The Committee at the same 
time also recommends  to Government of India that a separate fund may be 
earmarked for Ministry of HRD for opening of more ITIs throughout the country 
for producing secondary level engineers which are in great demand in the Capital 
Goods Industry.

off the interest and part of Government loan will not serve the purpose. The 


obsolete machines and technology needs to be replaced, work culture  has to be 
enforced. The Commi ttee hopes that DHI will do its best in this regard.

Coal Gasification Project:  
 
33. The Committee is surprised to find that despite its recommendations made in its 
208th report, there is no budgetary support made in this year BE -2010-11 for Coal 
gasification project sponsored by BHEL.  Last year, there was a token amount of Rs.1 
lakh fixed for this project and no p rovision was also made in the supplementary demand.  


The Committee has come to know that a private player is working on this project in their 
steel and power plant in Orissa by importing technology from South Africa due to non 
availability of this technology in the country.  The Secretary, DHI while deposing before 
the Committee stated that: "BHEL has a prestigious project of integrated coal expansion 
project.  It is a prime project which will lead to environment friendly power production 
technology in coll aboration with Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Company 
(APGENCO).  They are setting up a plant costing about Rs.1525 crore.  Since it is a 
project which has got a lot of potentiality in future in terms of generating power at lesser 
cost with more ecologica l friendly power generation using less fuel with the latest 
technology, we have been requesting that an amount of Rs.350 crore should be provided 
by the Government for their R&D with APGENCO providing Rs.854 crore and BHEL 
providing Rs.321 crore.  This has  not found a place in the Budget support".    Since this 
very important project has got lot of potentiality in future in terms of generating 
power at lesser cost with more eco -friendly power generation using less fuel with 
latest technology, the Committee r ecommends that in the national interest, 
protecting the ecology and generation cheaper power, the Government should 
provide the budgetary support of Rs. 350 crores for this all important project of 
BHEL at the RE stage so that the project is not got stalle d for want of funds because 
Government of India on the one hand is promoting/developing environment friendly 
projects and discouraging/shutting down polluting industries but on the other hand 
does not take serious interest on environment friendly power pro jects.  The country 
is facing acute power shortage and the capacity of this project is 182 MW.

OBSERVATIONS/ RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
AT A GLANCE  
 
The Committee is of the firm opinion that despite signs of a recovery of 
industrial growth during the period from October 2009 onwards, the performance 
of the industrial sector is cause of concern as the growth is directly proportional to 
stimulus packag es announced by the Government.  The Committee also expresses its 
concern on the sustainable growth of automobile sector in view of this years' 
budgetary proposals and hike in the excise duty of petroleum products.  The 
Committee feels that the need of the  hour is not merely in keeping on the stimulus 
packages but also to restructure the bases of taxes and import and export duties in 
such a manner that without affecting public expenditure, the industrial growth can 
sustain.  The Committee desires that this issue may be taken up with the Ministry of 
Finance and pursued seriously.  
(Para 5) 
 
The Committee appreciates that such an initiative of the Department of 
Heavy Industry with the Ministry of Urban Development will not only boost the 
demand in the Auto sect or but will also develop the public transport in the remote 
areas of the country.  The Committee, therefore, desires that the scheme of funding 
the purchase of buses for public transport by the States under JNNURM may 
continue for some more time in public interest.  The Committee at the same time, 
stresses upon the Department of Heavy Industry to monitor the progress of this 
scheme with the Ministry of Urban Development and concerned State Governments.  
(Para 7) 
 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the  Department of Heavy 
Industry should take up the issue with the Ministry of Finance to ensure 
concessional excise duty structure for utility vehicles.    
(Para 8) 
 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that in order to promote use of 
Hydrogen/Fuel cell/Hybri d vehicles, CNG vehicles and other alternative fuel 
vehicles, in the interest of protecting environment, such vehicles and its 


parts/components thereof may be exempted from excise duty at par with electric 
vehicles.   
(Para 9) 
 
The Committee feels that thi s policy will boost the auto sector during the 
coming years.  The Committee desires that Government should create a National 
Technology Development Fund for the development of auto and auto component 
industry.  This fund will not only provide impetus for m odernisation of auto sector 
but will also create huge employment opportunities in the country.  Further, this 
fund would provide financial support to companies by financing 50% of the project 
cost by way of a loan with minimum interest of 4 to 6%.  The Com mittee feels that 
such a fund will truly support auto companies to modernise and upgrade their 
technology in the globally competitive environment.  
(Para 10) 
 
The Committee, therefore, desires that Department of Heavy Industry 
should propose an amendment wi th Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) 
in Section 11 AB of the Central Excise Act, 1944 so that such anomalies may be 
sorted out. 
(Para 11) 
 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that Department of Heavy Industry 
should create a separate fund for th e upgradation of Auto Expo Centres like Pragati 
Maidan, Delhi etc. in consultation with ITPO and Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry.  The Committee further suggests the Department of Heavy Industry to 
also arrange such Auto Expos in other suitable places in t he country such as  
Greater Noida (U.P), Hyderabad (A.P.) and some other cities of the country where 
required infrastructure and facilities are available.  
(Para 12) 
 
The Committee wonders how the DHI will be able to complete the project with a 
meager Budg etary Support of Rs. 232.10 crore under BE 2010 -11.  The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the funds to the tune of Rs.654.90 crores shold be 
allocated to NATRIP which will be required for timely completion of this important 


national project which may be asked for during supplementary Demands for the 
year 2010-2011 so that funds asked for NATRIP are made available to complete the 
projects which are in pipeline.  
(Para 17) 
 
The Committee is surprised to know that despite of its serious concern for 
the re vival of Scooters India Ltd., the Department has made the provision of 
Budgetary support to this company to the tune of only Rs.4 crore which Committee 
feels is very meagre amount for its revival.  Committee,  therefore, recommends that 
the Department of H eavy Industry should make adequate Budgetary support for 
this company at the time of RE stage and at the same time, should seriously pursue 
its 70 crore rupee project proposal for revival through joint venture.  In fact, this 
important PSE has to diversify  its activities because it is manufacturing three 
wheelers which are being phased out in various parts of the Country. Mini four 
wheelers for transporting goods have fairly good market and with the help of 
Government this PSE may examine the diversificatio n issue in right earnest.  
(Para 18) 
 
The Committee feels that such imported machines/plants although imported 
at the lower cost but importers have to pay high prices for their maintenance 
contracts and spares.  The Committee notes that the DHI has raised s uch issue in 
the development council meeting.   The Committee recommends that suitable 
remedial measures be taken by imposing high import duty   and anti dumping duty 
on second hand machinery in consultation with Ministry of Commerce to grow our 
capital goods Industry.  The Committee impresses upon the Government to allocate 
sufficient fund for the engineering industry and R & D activities to sustain the 
Industrial growth in coming years.  
(Para 20) 
 
The Committee feels that the Department of Heavy Industry  needs to 
provide a road map to establish these clusters and provide adequate funds to create 
facilities for these clusters.  
(Para 21) 
 


The Committee feels that the DHI should facilitate such common facility 
centers in Public Private Participation (PPP) m ode.  Some of the Common facilities 
that can be provided are: -  
Common Foundry (for Machine Tool Industry);  
Common Heat Treatment facility (for Machine Tool Industry);  
Accredited Testing Laboratories;  
Design Centre; and  
Centers of Excellence  
 The Committ ee suggests that PPP based approach could be adopted for this 
purpose, under which group of entrepreneurs or industry associations would be 
encouraged. 
(Para 22) 
 
The Committee suggests that DHI should initiate action in this regard in 
coordination with Mi nistry of Railways, Road Transport & Highways and Ministry 
of Power etc.  
(Para 23) 
 
The Committee is of the view that the issue regarding   import duty should be 
discussed in details with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Ministry of 
Finance and Info rmation and Broadcasting before a decision is taken.  The 
Committee at the same time recommends that some measures need to be taken to 
protect the paper industry in the country.  The Committee also recommends that 
the issue regarding supply of Railway rake s on the M.G. Section linking Cachar 
Paper Mills to B.G. Section may be taken up with the Ministry of Railways so that 
speedy completion of conversion of meter gauge  can be made to help the paper 
industry in the North -Eastern region.  
(Para 24) 
 
The Committee expresses its serious concern over the state of affairs of HMT 
Ltd. Despite Governments grant of two revival packages in the recent past and part 
of the revival package is still under implementation. Despite these revival packages 
there is no turn aro und of the units. Department of Heavy Industry is contemplating 


for a Joint Venture and the Committee is of the opinion that serious attempts should 
be made for the revival of HMT Ltd. through the Joint Venture route as a last 
resort otherwise how long the  public money can be pumped and drained in keeping 
the PSE alive. In that eventuality some other options including closure have to be 
given a serious thought.   The Committee, therefore, is of the view that necessary 
budgetary support should be given for th e upgradation of technology to HMT Ltd. 
during supplementary demands 2010 -2011.  The Government should at the same 
time also impress upon bulk buyers in the Government Sector, such as Railways, 
Indian Airlines, Commonwealth Games Organization Committee etc .  to opt, 
wherever  feasible, for HMT products so that this once much achieved and 
prestigious unit would come out of the red.  
(Para 25) 
 
The Committee has made its serious concern on its long waiting list for 
establishment of power plants in the country . Committee finds that it has a pending 
list for customers who are waiting for 2 -3 years. 
(Para 26) 
 
The Committee is of the view that fierce competition to BHEL from these 
companies is healthy kind of thing which improves the performance of BHEL day 
by da y. The Committee at the same time feels that Capital Goods Industry faces 
dearth of skilled and trained manpower both at shop floor level, as well as 
managerial level. With growing demand and growth of Capital Goods Industry it 
needs to be provided with ad equate skilled manpower. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that DHI should consider providing the Industry with assistance for 
development of skills to employees of PSUs through approved training institutes.  
For this purpose exclusive Industrial Traini ng Institutes may be established for 
BHEL or arrangements may be made with various ITIs to train batches of students 
in these vocations for BHEL. The Committee finds that no budgetary support has 
been provided to engineering sector and there is huge demand  of secondary level 
engineers in the Capital Goods Sector. The Committee therefore recommends that 
BHEL themselves, meet various engineering clusters and support it through various 
up gradation schemes. The Committee at the same time also recommends to 


Government of India that a separate fund may be earmarked for Ministry of HRD 
for opening of more ITIs throughout the country for producing secondary level 
engineers which are in great demand in the Capital Goods Industry.   
(Para 26) 
 
The Committee is of the  view that there must be some practical difficulties in 
the revival packages of loss making PSUs, Committee finds that DHI proposes the 
revival plan, starts preparing project reports, finalize these reports which consume 
lot of time and therefore before it s execution, due to fast changing latest technology 
and global modernization, the whole revival package suggested by the DHI becomes 
outdated. Hence, the revival packages have to be prepared and implemented in a 
time bound manner by removing the red tape a nd other bottlenecks.  The 
Committee feels that there is a great deal of uncertainty in regard to the public 
sector enterprises such as Scooters India Ltd., HMT etc. The Committee impress 
upon the Government that where budgetary support becomes too difficu lt, the 
Ministry of Finance should be approached to arrange for adequate funds from 
banks and other financial institution under stipulated conditions.  
(Para 30) 
 
 The Committee desires that apart from the sickness of the PSUs under the 
Department of Heavy  Industry, DHI should focus its concern on the modernization 
of all the PSUs so that they may face the competition in the market. The Committee, 
recommends, that the revival of PSUs too should be in real terms and simply writing 
off the interest and part o f Government loan will not serve the purpose. The 
obsolete machines and technology needs to be replaced, work culture  has to be 
enforced. The Committee hopes that DHI will do its best in this regard.  
 
(Para 31) 
 
The Committee notes with concern that major part of the financial packages 
are in the form of writing off the interest and loans and funds are not provided for 
modernisation, technology upgradation etc.  The Committee hopes that the 


Department will focus on the modernisation of the PSUs instead of s imply waiving 
off the loans, interests etc.  
(Para 32) 
Since this very important project has got lot of potentiality in future in terms 
of generating power at lesser cost with more eco -friendly power generation using 
less fuel with latest technology, the C ommittee recommends that in the national 
interest, protecting the ecology and generation cheaper power, the Government 
should provide the budgetary support of Rs. 350 crores for this all important 
project of BHEL at the RE stage so that the project is not got stalled for want of 
funds because Government of India on the one hand is promoting/developing 
environment friendly projects and discouraging/shutting down polluting industries 
but on the other hand does not take serious interest on environment friendly  power 
projects.  The country is facing acute power shortage and the capacity of this 
project is 182 MW.   
 (Para 33) 
 
The Committee finds that the progress made by various CPSE in respect of 
recruitment of SCs/STs/OBCs/Minorities is not very encouraging.  The Committee 
feels that HR Department of these PSUs should be very particular at the time of 
recruitment of manpower in their PSUs in respect of SCs/STs/OBCs/Miniority etc 
candidates.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that particular care be taken so  
that the reserved quotas are filled and a periodical assessment on a continuous basis 
is undertaken for this purpose.  
 (Para 36) 
The Committee hopes that its recommendations will be taken in the right 
earnest to promote the heavy industrial sector and mor e so the auto sector, capital

REPORT 
 
 
 The Department of Public Enterprises (of the Ministry of Heavy Industries and 
Public Enterprises) is the nodal department for all Central Public Sector Enterprises 
(CPSEs) and formulates policy pertaining to the role of CPSEs in the economy and also 
lays down policy guidelines for performance improvement, autonomy and financial 
delegation, personnel management and other related areas.  The DPE is also the interface 
between the administrative Ministries and the CPSEs.  
 
2. There are approximately 246 PSUs out of which 213 are functional, these 246 
PSUs are distributed among 38 different Min istries.  So, it is a vast colla ge of enterprises 
distributed among different sections of the Government. 
 
3. The intention of the Government in creating the DPE was to f ind an enabling 
mechanism which would be able to coordinate and which would also bring some 
cohesion as to where and in what direction the public enterprises should move and how 
there could also be an independent third party evaluation of these PSEs.   
  
 The Department tries to continuously improve the management of PSEs by way 
of professionalization  of the management, goal setting and reviewing performance of 
PSEs, evolving guidelines for corporate governance and social responsibility and 
strengthening the institutional mechanism for revival of sick units. 
  
4. As per the Allocation of Business Rules of the Central Government, the following 
subjects have been allocated to the Department of Public Enterprises:- 
 
(i) Co-ordination of matters of general policy o f non -financial nature 
affecting all public sector industrial and commercial undertakings. 
(ii) Matters relating to Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) mechanism of 
improving the performance of Public Sector Undertakings. 
(iii) Matters relating to Permanent Machinery o f Arbitration for the Public 
Sector Enterprises. 
(iv) Matter relating to Counselling, Retraining and Redeployment of 
employees in Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) under 
Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS).  
 
“The Committee desires that in order to play a meaningful and effective role 
in getting the policies and guidelines implemented by the PSEs the Department of 
Public Enterprises should ask for the compliance report from the PSEs about the 
implementation of the policies and guidelines formulated by it from time to time and 
separate paragraph thereon may be incorporated in the Annual Report of the 
Ministry”.  
 
5. The Department of Public Enterprises has been provided an allocation of Rs. 
15.72 crores for 2010 -11.  The Plan expenditure is Rs. 10.50 crores  whereas Non -Plan 
expenditure is 5.22. crores.  The allocation for current year 2010-11 is slightly higher by  
 
 


Rs. 1.64  crores  as compared to  RE 2009-10.   The major Plan  expenditure of   Rs. 7.85  
crores is on account of the CRR Scheme for rationali zed employees and VRS optess of 
CPSEs.  The Plan expenditure for Information Technology is Rs. 60 lakhs and Rs. 1.00 
crore for the Scheme of Research, Development and Consultancy on generic issues 
related to CPSEs and SLPEs. The provision for projects/sche mes for NE region is Rs. 
1.05 crores which is 10% of the total plan expenditure.

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ( MoU) 
 
26. The MoU system has started several years ago and it has become robust and 
entrenched over the last 3-4 years.  The PSEs and their mother Ministries are subscribing 
to the MoUs.  The MoUs are made at the b eginning of the performance year in which 
targets are set which are measurable, quantifiable and could be monitored. 
 
27. The Secretary of the DPE informed that earlier the MoU was signed between the 
mother Ministry and the CPSE and because of relationship  that existed between them 
often soft targets were being set for own CPSEs.  Now, the DPE being a third party it 
takes an objective view of the performance and try to set benchmarks that are not only 
limited to that particular enterprises but related to the industry across where it operates. 
 
 
 
9 
 


28. The evaluation of the performance of MoU is done at the end of the year in which 
mother Ministry and the CPSE sit in conjunction with the Task Force of DPE consisting 
of 5-6 experts in finance, domain experts,  retired bureaucrats etc.  In the evaluation 50% 
marks are given for the financial performance and 50% for non -financial performance 
such as corporate social responsibility, sustainable development, human resource etc. on 
that basis PSEs are graded as excellent, very good, good etc.

pertaining to MoU between the PSEs and the administrative Ministries, the Committee 
noted that 144 PSEs in 2007 -08, 147 PSEs in 2008 -09 and 197 PSEs in 2009-10 had 
signed MoU.

separate paragraph thereon may be incorporated in the Annual Report of the 
Ministry.  
(Para 4) 
 
The Committee  observes that the actual expenditure  for both Planned and 
Non-Planned, have been less than the RE for the year  2008-09 in various heads.  The 
Committee desires to know from the Department of Public Enterprises regarding  
expenditure indicated by the DPE fo r the year 2009 -10 upto 31.03.2010 for both 
Planned and Non -Planned expenditure. The Committee is of the considered view 
that Department can do much better if it can anticipate the needs and requirements  
of future and have an eye on past development while  making budgetary allocation 
for various schemes and programmes being run by it .  
(Para 14) 
 
 The Committee, therefore, recommends that Department should ensure full 
utilisation of funds allocated and efforts should also be made that it is evenly 
distributed in different quarters.  This will result in effective implementation of the 
various schemes.  
(Para 15) 
 
The Committee observes that most of the PSEs for which revival has been 
recommended by the BRPSE and a ssistance recommended from GOI  belong to the 
capital goods sector under Department of Heavy Industry. The Committee 
expresses its serious concern over the costly revivals that largely entail waivers and 
conversions of the secured loans and interest dues towards Government of India.  
The Committee desir es to know from the DPE about fresh cash infusions for 
modernisation and technology upgradation of the sick PSEs and how much would 
be in the form of secured loans, unsecured equity and grants respectively, PSE -wise.  
The Committee also seeks information r egarding the steps taken to secure the 
Government loans and interest thereon.  
(Para 17) 
 
The Committee recommends that once a revival package is approved by the 
competent authority, the responsibility of justifying the revival package should be 
on the adm inistrative Ministries. The BRPSE should suggest measures to secure 
Government’s investments in the form of unsecured equity.  
(Para 18) 
 
17 


The Committee is of the view that BRPSE should explore the feasibility of 
entrusting the task of looking after sick  organisation to a healthy organisation for its 
turnaround as has been done in the case of BHPV, Eastern Coalfields etc.  
(Para 23) 
The Committee feels that there should be sense of urgency in dealing with 
revival cases and definite time frame should be fix ed and adhered to.  
(Para 24) 
 
The Committee once again recommends that BRPSE should try its best to 
give timely recommendations either for revival or closure but the issue should not  
linger on indefinitely.   
(Para 25) 
The Committee notes that the perform ance of CPSEs is evaluated on the 
basis of achievement against the MoU targets. The Committee observes that there is 
a decreasing trend in the `Excellent ’ rating in the year 2008 -09 as compared to the 
year 2007 -08.  The Committee, therefore, recommends tha t this decreasing trend 
should be dispelled by creating suitable atmosphere for CPSEs by the concerned 
administrative Ministr ies.   
(Para 35) 
 
The Committee observes that though numbers of PSEs signing the MoU is 
increasing and it is highest (197) in the y ear 2009-10 and evaluated rating 
‘Excellent’ in 2007 -08 was 55 only which decreased to 47 in 2008 -09.  The 
Committee would like to have the comments of DPE on this development  of 
excellent rating going down .  The Committee recommends that the Department ma y 
persuade remaining PSUs to sign MoU.  
(Para 36) 
The Committee takes note of the efforts made by the DPE and desires that it 
should be apprise d of the responses of the performance of sick and loss making 
PSEs during 2004 -05 to 2008 -09.  The Committee also desires that DPE  should 
study the reasons of sickness of PSEs and find out their revival strategies , in right 
earnest.  
(Para 37) 
The Committee observes the variations of VRS optees in each year, and notes that 
the Plan outlay has been curtailed due to les ser availability of V RS optees in CPSEs. 
However, the Committee feels that the details of n umber of the trainees covered 
under CRR Scheme and n umber of trainees redeployed is to be provided to the 
Committee for appraisal . The Committee hopes that the DPE would furnish the 
updated details to the Committee  in this regard.  
(Para 46) 
 
The Committee desires that DPE should ensure that funds earmarked under 
CRR Scheme and Research, Development and Consultancy on Generic issue related 
to CPSEs must be utilized eq ually in each quarter.  
 (Para 47) 
 
 
18 


The Committee find s that n o information has been provided regarding the 
expenditure incurred for the training modules since last three years.  The 
Committee desires that year-wise detail of expenditure incurred on ea ch training 
modules shall be provided to it at the earliest .  
(Para 48) 
 
The Committee finds that VRS is being implemented not only by the sick and 
loss making PSEs but also by the profit making PSEs in order to rationalise and 
reduce their manpower in the  hope that it will turn around the PSE or further 
increase its profits substantially.  But neither the concerned PSE nor the 
Government i.e. the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Department of Public 
Enterprises or the Ministry under whose jurisdiction th e concerned PSE falls bother 
for the future of the employee opting for VRS or in many cases are forced to opt for 
VRS because after some time for various reasons the money received by optees is 
finished and no source for living is left with them.  They are  forced to live a pathetic 
life with all sorts of miseries.  To avoid this Counselling, Retraining and 
Redeployment (CRR) Scheme assumes importance.  The Committee desires that 
more and more employees of PSEs should be retained and their redeployment 
should be ensured in other PSEs as per their demand because skilled manpower is 
very much in demand.  VRS should be the last option.  The Committee also desires 
that a survey may be conducted to know the condition of VRS optees of various 
PSEs and welfare measu res be extended to them.  
(Para 49) 
 
The Committee recommends that DPE should issue guidelines to the SLPSEs 
asking them to furnish the information on their performance well in time for 
preparing the next Annual Survey of SLPSEs and also take up the matter  with State 
Governments to nominate one Department as the Nodal Department for dat a 
compilation on SLP SEs. 
(Para 52) 
 
The Committee find s that the problems faced by SLPSEs such as absence of 
Board of Directors, short tenure of CMDs and lack of both operati onal and strategic 
autonomy (for making investment)  are due to lack of coordination between the State 
Government and SLPSEs and recommends that  DPE should prepare  a well 
articulated model MoU to be signed between State Government and SLPSEs for 
improving the performance of SLPSEs.  
(Para 53) 
 
The Committee has noted and appreciates the views of the SCOPE.  
 
(Para 56) 
 
 
19 
 


The Committee noted the retention of Rs. 1.00 crore  for North-Eastern Region .  The 
Committee, recommends that the Department should mak e efforts to utilise the 
funds instead of simply let them transfer to non -lapsable pool.  
(Para 59) 
 
The Committee has discussed the issue of professionalization of Boards of 
PSUs many times in the recent past and has also made recommendations with 
regard thereto but expresses its concern that its recommendations have  not been 
implemented in letter and spirit.  In the name of independent  Directors only retired 
bureaucrats are being accommodated in the Board.  There is no compulsory 
induction of Directors f rom the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBC and 
women categories to take care of at least the employees of these categories of the 
PSUs.  Even the former Members of Parliament are not appointed as Directors to 
have the benefit of their vast public life  experience.  So is the case of vast majority of 
shareholders of the CPSEs.  The present norms of professionalization of Boards are 
certainly not satisfactory.  The   Committee desires that D epartment of Public 
Enterprises may come out with a proposal for amending the guidelines in this 
regard so that the Directors representing the SCs, STs, OBCs and ex -MPs and a 
public share holder can get the opportunity to become independent  Director s.  For 
this purpose educational qualification and experience should be p rescribed. 
 
(Para 60) 
 
At the same time the Committee recommends that in order to play a 
meaningful role in the affairs of CPSEs the Department of Public Enterprises 
should not remain a mere interface between the administrative Ministries and the 
CPSEs and  therefore the Department should be entrusted with the power of 
nominating one non official and knowledgeable person as Director in the Board of 
every CPSE.  
(Para 61) 
 
The Committee further recommend s that selection of CMDs of various PSUs 
should be done quickly by Public Enterprises Selection Board without any delay 
and with transparency.  It is quite surprising that the Department of Public 
Enterprises and Public Enterprises Selection Board do not play any role in selecting 
and  appointing the CMDs and  EDs  and  Directors  in the Boards  of  Public Sector  
 
(Para 62) 
 
The Committee also finds that various posts of SCs/STs/OBC are lying 
vacant in PSUs since quite long and directs that DPE should take appropriate 
measures to fill them soon as per the guide lines of GOI in this regard.  
(Para 63) 
 
The Committee hopes that its recommendations will be well taken up by the 
Department of Public Enterprises in view of the recent scenario of the industrial 
sector of the country.  
(Para 64)

Out of this, the gross budgetary support accounts for Rs. 24400.00 crore, whereas Rs. 150.00

In addition, NSIC is expected to generate IEBR to the tune of Rs. 150.00 crore. 
 
3. The MSME sector constitutes a vibrant segment of the Indian economy contributing 
significantly to the manufacturing output, employment and national exports. The primary 
responsibility for promotion and development of MSMEs lies with State Government.  
However, the Government of India has always taken active interest in supplementing the 
efforts of the State Governments.  The role of the Ministry of MSME is mainly to assist the 
States in the ir efforts to promote growth and development of MSMEs, for enhancing the 
competitiveness of these enterprises in an increasingly market -led economy and for 
generating additional employment opportunities.  In addition, the Ministry also attempts to 
address the common concerns of these enterprises.  
   
4. According to the estimates of 4 th All -India Census of MSMEs,  the number of 
enterprises is  about 26 million and these provide employment to an estimated 60 million 
persons Of the 26 million MSMEs, only 1.5 m illion are in the registered segment while the 
remaining 24.5 million (94%) are in the unregistered segment. MSMEs  are estimated to  
contribute 8 per cent of the country’s GDP, 45 per cent of the manufactured output and 40 per 
cent of our exports. 
  
5. The most significant contribution of the MSME sector lies in creation of larger 
employment opportunities at lower capital cost. The labour and capital ratio in MSMEs and 
the overall growth in the MSMEs is much higher than in the larger industries. MSMEs are 
better dispersed. In view of these factors, MSMEs are important for achieving national 
objectives of growth with equity and inclusion. 
   


 7 
6. On a query  to the various initiatives taken in the wake of global economic slowdown, 
for the promotion and developme nt of MSMEs and to enhance their competitiveness, it was   
informed that  the Government continued with its thrust on the implementation of the major 
schemes/programmes during 2009 -10, which included Credit Guarantee Scheme, Credit 
Linked Capital Subsidy S cheme, Performance and Credit Rating Scheme, Cluster 
Development Programme, Prime Minister ’s Employment Generation programme and Market 
Development Assistance Scheme.   New schemes under the National Manufacturing 
Competitiveness Programme were also introdu ced.  In the Union Budget 2009 -10, a special 
fund of Rs.4,000 crore has been provided to SIDBI to incentivise Banks and State Financial 
Corporations (SFCs) to lend to MSEs and to facilitate the flow of credit at reasonable rates to 
the sector.  The measure s for protecting and providing a stimulus to the MSMEs were taken 
by the Government, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Public Sector Banks in view of 
the impact of global recession on MSMEs,   
 
7. A High Level Task Force under the chairmanship of the  Principal Secretary to the 
Prime Minister was constituted to address the issues of MSME sector which has since 
submitted its report.  The Ministry of MSME has initiated necessary action for implementing 
the recommendations in a time-bound manner.   
 
8. During the discussions with the various associations of MSME sector the associations 
impressed upon the Committee to ensure the implementation of the recommendations of the 
Task Force which will immensely help them to address to their problems and also help in 
advancement and growth of the MSME sector.   
 
9. The Committee, therefore recommends that the recommendations of the Task 
Force should be implemented in letter and spirit on priority basis.  
  
10. The various policy measures/initiatives and thrust on augmenting credit delivery to the 
sector have resulted in increasing  the outstanding credit to micro and small enterprises (MSE) 
sector from the Public Sector Banks from Rs. 1,85,626  crore as at the end of March 2009 and 
to Rs.2,44,104 crore at the end of September 2009.     
 
11. The Action Plan for the Ministry for the year 2010-11 is as under: 
 
· Implementation of the recommendations of the Task Force on MSMEs in a time 
bound manner; 
· Facilitate credit flow to the MSME Sector – by implementing the credit rel ated 
Scheme for MSEs through banks/financial institutions; 
· Providing impetus to the Cluster Development Programme. 
· Implementation of the components/schemes formulated under the National 
Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme; 
· Generation of more employment  opportunities by providing thrust on implementation 
of Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme. 
· Strengthening of the Khadi sector through implementation of ADB -assisted Khadi 
Reform Development Package.   
· Set up a Info-call centre for MSMEs. 
· Focus and upscale entrepreneurship & skill development programme. 
 


 8 
12. The Ministry apprised that s ubsequent to enactment of "Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises Development Act, 2006", the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries and Ministry 
of Small Scale Indu stries were merged into a single Ministry, namely, “Ministry of Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises.” This merger has resulted in better coordination and synergy 
in implementation of various programmes/schemes being implemented by various 
organisations/institutions under the Ministry. The present organizational set up has been 
effective and efficient in achieving the targets set out for the Ministry.  
 
13. Since the issues pertaining to MSMEs involve multiple stakeholders in and outside the 
Government, the Ministry and its organisational units have focused on building awareness, 
motivation, capacities and consensus at all levels.  Such efforts will be continued in the 
forthcoming years also. 
 
14. Ministry of MSME had projected a sum of Rs.3118.65 crore for t he year 2010-11 as 
detailed below. Planning Commission after discussion with this Ministry fixed the annual 
plan 2010 -11 outlay at Rs.2400 crore. This represents 34% increase in outlay over the 
previous year.   The major reduction  vis-à-vis the projected d emand is under the scheme of 
Quality of Technology Support Institutions and Programmes, Credit  Support Programme,  
Khadi Grant (including MDA for Khadi), Village Industries Grant and Prime Minister ’s

15. About the  major policy shift for the year 2010 -11 as compared to 2009 -10 in respect 
of the schemes being implemented by the Ministry of MSME it was informed that there is no 
policy shift . However, in line with the recommenda tions made by the Task Force on

providing an impetus to the growth of the MSME sector as also facilitate in enhancing its 
contribution to the overall economy. 
 
16. Regarding  the impact of global economic slowdown on MSMEs, the Government, the 
RBI and the Public Sector Banks have announced several measures for protecting and 
providing a stimulus to the MSMEs. These, inter alia, include:  
 
(a) Stimulus Package announced on 7 th December 2008 
· Cenvat cut of 4 percentage points  on all products for t he remainder of the financial 
year (other than petroleum and those products for which the current rate is less than 
4%). 
· 2% interest rate subvention in pre -and post -shipment credit for small and medium 
enterprises sector. 
· Guarantee cover under Credit Guara ntee Scheme for Micro and Small enterprises on 
loans will be extended from Rs.50 lakh to Rs.1 crore with a guarantee cover of 50%. 
· Lock-in period for loans  covered under the existing Credit Guarantee Scheme will be 
reduced from 24 to 18 months. 
· Government to issue an advisory to central public sector enterprises and request state 
public sector enterprises to ensure prompt payment of bills of MSMEs.  
(b) Stimulus Package announced on 2 nd January 2009 
· Special monthly meetings of State Level Bankers ’ Committee s would be held to 
oversee the resolution of credit issues of MSMEs by banks. Ministry of MSME and 
Department of Financial Services will jointly set up a cell to monitor the progress on 
this front.  
· To enhance the flow of credit to micro enterprises, the g uarantee cover extended by 
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust will be increased to 85% for credit facility up to Rs.5 
lakh.  
 
 The Committee is of the firm opinion that these stimulus packages of the 
Government have immensely helped the MSME sector to withstand t he worst of 
the recession in the world economy and in the over all interest of this sector these 
packages needs to be continued for some more time at least till the recession is 
completely over.  Even if the Government intends to withdraw them in fur tre 
these should be gradually withdrawn and certainly not in one go.  
  
(c) Measures announced by the Reserve Bank of India  
· Refinance limit of Rs.7,000 crore to Small Industries Development Bank of India 
(SIDBI) for incremental on -lending to the MSE sector, dire ctly or through banks, 
NBFCs and SFCs. 
· Banks have been advised to contribute an aggregate amount of Rs.2000 crore to the 
MSME Refinance Fund with SIDBI. 
· As a one time measure, the second restructuring done by banks of exposures up to 
June 30, 2009, will also be eligible for exceptional regulatory treatment. 
· While sanctioning/renewing credit limits to their large corporate borrowers, banks 
have been advised to fix separate sub -limits, within the overall limits, specifically for 
meeting payment obligations in respect of purchases from MSEs. 
 
 
 


 10 
(d) Measures announced by the Public Sector Banks  
· Public Sector Banks to grant need based adhoc Working Capital Demand Loans up to 20% of 
the existing fund based limits in respect of units having overall fund based credit facility up to 
Rs.10 crore. 
· Reducing interest rates for borrowing by micro industries by 1% (for all existing and new 
loans) and in respect of SMEs where banks have fund based exposures up to Rs.10 crore by 
0.5%. 
· Moratorium period will be extended in res pect of loans availed by MSMEs where project 
implementation has been delayed in the current scenario. 
· Finance for purchase of gensets will be made available on soft terms. 
· Public Sector Banks will set up Regional MSME Care Centres to facilitate MSME 
entrepreneurs for quick disposal of their grievances. The functioning of these Centres will be 
monitored directly by the Head Office and the list of these Centres will be posted on IBA 
portal and on the web site of each public sector bank.   
 
17.  The Committee has been informed that the Ministry of MSME has undertaken necessary 
modifications under the Credit Guarantee Scheme. The Ministry has also set up a ‘MSME Credit 
Monitoring Cell ’ to oversee the resolution of credit issues of MSMEs by banks. Further, the 
Government has issued an  advisory to central public sector enterprises and has requested the State 
Governments to issue a similar advisory to the State Public Sector Enterprises and Electricity Boards 
to ensure prompt payment of bills of MSMEs. To ensure tha t large numbers of MSMEs benefit 
through the various measures announced, the Government is closely monitoring the implementation in 
consultation with the State/UT Governments. As per reports received, most of the States/UTs are 
holding regular meetings of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC)/special SLBC to review the 
flow of credit to the MSME sector, restructuring of MSME accounts under stress, prompt payments of 
dues to MSEs by the large units, etc. The review mechanism through SLBC has helped considerably in 
addressing the liquidity problems faced by the MSME sector. 
          The Committee desires that the members of this Committee from State may also be invited 
in the meetings of SLBC of that particular State because of their vast knowledge about MSME 
sector which will immensely help the SLBC in this regard .  
 
18. The Ministry of MSME has not conducted any specific survey to assess the impact of 
recession on MSMEs. However, Labour Bureau (M/o Labour & Employment) has conducted five 
quarterly quick employment surveys to assess the effect of economic slowdown on employment 
in the country during the quarters October. -December, 2008, January -March, 2009, April -June, 
2009, July-September, 2009 and October -December, 2009.  Based on these surveys, the sect or-

20. As per the sample survey conducted by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, the 
most affected sectors were Gems & Jewellery, Textiles, Transport and Automobiles, where

oriented units.  
   
21. The Committee was informed that  facilitate the promotion and development of micro, 
small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and enhance their competitiveness, the Government 
had announced a ‘Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to Small and Medium Enterprises 
(SMEs)’ in August 2005 which envisages public sector banks  to fix their own targets for 
funding MSMEs in order to achieve a minimum 20 per cent year -on-year growth in credit to 
the MSME sector.  The Government had also announced in February 2007 a ‘Package for 
Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises ’ with an obj ective to provide support in areas of 
credit, technology upgradation, marketing, infrastructure, etc. Further, keeping in view the 
impact of global economic slowdown on MSMEs, the Government, the Reserve Bank of India 
(RBI) and the Public Sector Banks have taken several measures for protecting and providing a 
stimulus to the MSMEs.   
 
22. On being asked about the implementation of ‘Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to 
Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) ’ the Committee was informed that it involved action 
on the part of RBI and the Banks. The RBI issued circular dated 19 August 2005 to all the 
public sector banks and 25 August 2005 to all private sector banks/ foreign banks/ RRBs, 
advising them to implement the measures announced in the Policy Package. Un der the 
‘Package for Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises’, the Ministry of MSME was required 
to initiate action for extending the support to MSEs as envisaged beside effecting necessary 
modifications in the schemes/programmes. As already mentioned, so me of the measures 
announced in the stimulus package like modifications in the Credit Guarantee Scheme, setting 
up of a Cell to attend to matters remaining unresolved with the Banks - SME Helpline, taking 
up with the State Governments for issuing advisory to State Public Sector Enterprises to 
ensure prompt payment of bills of MSMEs, convening special monthly meetings of State 
Level Bankers ’ Committee, etc. involved action on the part of Ministry of MSME. The 
Ministry had already taken the action in the matter. 
 
23. Despite the tall claims referred to above the factual position is otherwise.  One of the 
office bearer, a woman entrepreneur, while making submission before the Committee said “as 
industrialists’ we find that the attitude of the banker is changing .  Earlier the industrialists 
were treated as angels and we were given a red carpet welcome by the bankers.  Now due to 
global crisis we are treated like devils.  Even the recommendation relating to collateral free 
loan upto five lakh rupees is only on pap ers and has not been followed.  “This submission 
shows how difficult it is for the MSME sector to get credit from the Banks.  Apart from this 


 12 
the MSME associations were expecting for lower rate of interest of the Banks on subsidized 
rates on the lines of agriculture sector.   But their hopes have been dashed.   
 
  The Committee, therefore, recommends that Ministry of MSME should take up 
the issues of credit problems and subsidized rates of interest at par with agriculture 
sector for MSME sector with the Min istry of Finance and Reserve Bank of India in right 
earnest so that the entrepreneurs of MSME sector get hassle free loans from the Banks 
and they too are given the benefit of subsidized rate of interest on their Bank loans.  The 
Committee expects that it will be informed about the outcome in this regard.

25. The Government of India launched the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Micro and 
Small Enterprises in August, 2000, with the objective of making available cr edit to micro and 
small enterprises (MSEs), particularly micro enterprises, without collateral/third party 
guarantees.  The Scheme is being operated through the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro 
and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) set up jointly by the Gove rnment of India and Small 
Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). 
 
26. The Scheme covers collateral free credit facility (term loan and/or working capital) 
extended by eligible member lending institutions (MLIs) to new and existing micro and small 
enterprises up to Rs. 100 lakh per borrowing unit.  The guarantee cover provided is up to 75% 
of the credit facility up to Rs. 50 lakh with an incremental guarantee of 50% of the credit 
facility above Rs. 50 lakh and up to Rs. 100 lakh (85% for loans up to R s. 5 lakh provided to 
micro enterprises, 80% for MSEs owned/operated by women and all loans to domicile of 
NER).  One time guarantee fee of 1.5% of the credit facility sanctioned (0.75% for NER) and 
Annual Service Fee of 0.75% is collected from the MLIs.

46. Sickness amongst the MSME units is a cause of concern.  Several reasons account for 
the sickness in this vital sector.  Delayed payment is  one of the factors.  The MSMEs do not 
get their payment from their clients for years.  Government appointed a facilitation Council 
for arbitration in such cases whose decision is binding on both the parties but the bigger 
players do not bother for the decisions of the Council and a small unit has no resources to 
fight court cases in such cases.  Now after the Micro, Small and Medium E nterprises 
Development Act, 2006 come into force a ray of hope is there for this sector regarding 
delayed payments.   The Committee was informed that there is no appropriate Rehabilitation 
Scheme  for the sick units of MSME sector, Securitization law is also playing a havoc because 
if for some reason SSI uni t is unable to repay the loan or  instalments for three months the 
account become NPA and a simple notice closes the unit itself.  The associations have 
demanded that the NPA period should be at least one year which means if the  default is for 
one year then only the account should become NPA.  The Committee desires that  this 
demand should be considered sympathetically by the Government.  The Committee was 
also informed that earlier it was seller market fo r the products of MSME sectors but now it is 
buyers market.  A small enterprenurers cannot go to places to sell his product.  For this 
creation of marketing companies or agencies has been demanded and The Committee desires 
that this demand too should be co nsidered favo urably.  The associations also complaint 
about strict regulatory regime, ambit of number of Central and State Acts and inspection of 
number of inspectors and capability of every inspector to close the unit is hampering the 
growth of this vital sector.  Some time the inspector humiliate the entrepreneur in front of his 
worker.  The associations demanded removal inspector raj.  There should be a compendium of  
all labour laws and there should be only one inspector to see the compliance of the law s.  The 
entrepreneurs are also harassed in the name of surveys and raids and also humiliated.  The 
Ministry should take note of all this complaints.

58. The Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC), established under the Khadi and 
Village Industries Commission Act, 1956, is a statutory organization engaged in promoting 
and developing khadi and village industries for providing employment opportunities in rural 
areas, thereby strengthening the rural eco nomy.  The KVIC has been identified as one of the 
major organizations in the decentralized sector for generating sustainable rural non -farm 
employment opportunities at low per capita investment.  This also helps in checking 
migration of rural population to  urban areas in search of the employment opportunities.  It 
undertakes activities like skill improvement; transfer of technology; research & development; 
marketing etc. and helps in generating employment/self -employment opportunities in rural 
areas.    The following are the schemes in implemented by KVIC.

(ii) Khadi Grant including Marketing Development Assistance for Khadi 
(iii) Village Industries Grant 
(iv) Workshed Scheme for Khadi Artisans 
(v) Interest  Subsidy (Khadi) 
(vi) Interest Subsidy (Village Industries) 
(vii) Schme for enhancing productivity and competitiveness of Khadi Industries and 
Artisans 
(viii) Strengthening of infrastructure of existing weak khadi institutions and 
assistance for marketing infrastructure. 
(ix) Khadi Reform and Development Programme (ADB Assistance).

67. Khadi is a fabric for the masses, even today.  It consists almost all the items of textiles, 
particularly home-apparel.  Khadi can cater to people of all categories, rural and urban, rich 
and poor, starting from lungi/towels, dhotis to costly silk sarees.   However, khadi is a healthy 
and eco -friendly fabric and above all, a heritage fabric.  Although, in the changing 
environment, khadi is being positioned as a fabric for the niche segment, maximum return is 
ensured for the rural artisans engaged in the activity.  We have to bear in mind that input costs 
are escalating.  Since khadi provide employment to most vulnerable sections of the society to 
ensure a fair wage, cost of khadi becomes high and needs support. 
 
68. Khadi activity, is undertaken with the principle of ‘No’ profit ‘No’ loss.  The Central 
Certification Committee constituted by KVIC, keeps close vigil on the price line of khadi.  
Moreover, khadi uses only natural raw -materials like cotton, wool and silk, which are pure 
and comparatively expensive than cheaper bended raw -materials used by textile mills.  Also, 
khadi production is entirely labour intensive and this process, also adds to the cost. 
 
69. In order to sustain the Khadi sector in the country the committee recommends 
that all the Ministries, Departments, PSEs and ot her organizations should opt for Khadi 
items for curtains of doors and windows, dusters, towels, dress material for the 
employees and give their annual requirements to KVIC.  This will certainly boost the 
Khadi sector.

90. The Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate (ISEC) Scheme is an important mechanism 
of funding khadi programme by khadi institutions.  It was introduced in May 1977 to mobilise 
funds from banking institutions for filling the gap between the actual fund requirements and 
availability of funds from budgetary sources.  
 
91. Under the ISEC Scheme, credit at the concessional rate of interest of 4% per annum 
for capital expenditure as well as working capital, is made available as per the requirement of 
the institutions.  The difference between the actual lending rate and 4% is paid by the Central 
Government through KVIC to the lending banks and funds for this purpose are provided 
under the khadi grant head to KVIC. 
 
92. Margin Money Subsidy to the tune of Rs.408.65 crore against the target of Rs.740 
crore could actually be di sbursed by Banks to the beneficiaries during 2008 -09.  The reason 
for shortfall in disbursement of Margin Money is because PMEGP does not envisage a simple 
transfer of subsidy to the beneficiary. Selection, training, deposit of own contribution,  
permission from statutory authorities, establishment of backward - forward linkages,  


 28 
enthusiasm and readiness of banks  to quickly release the loan amount /subsidy etc. are pre -
requisites for speedy utilization of funds.  
 
93. We have switched over from the system  of treating release of subsidy to nodal banks 
against sanctioned cases as utilization of funds that was prevalent under the earlier REGP 
scheme to a more challenging system of release of funds to implementing agencies only 
against actual transfer of subsi dy to beneficiary accounts in the financing bank branches, 
under PMEGP. Stricter financial discipline and proper appreciation of this requirement by 
implementing agencies and financing / nodal bank branches in particular were required, which 
took time. Pil ot project for establishing ‘one bank one nodal branch ’ concept to reduce the 
time taken in release of funds to the beneficiaries has also been discussed with selected banks 
for improving the performance.

123. The Coir Board is a statutory body established under the Coir Industry Act, 1953 for 
promoting overall development of the coir industry and improving the living conditions of the 
workers engaged in the traditional industry. The coir industry employs more than 6.50 lakh 
persons of whom majority is from rural areas belonging to the economically weaker sections 
of society.  Nearly 80%  of the coir workers in the fibre extract ion and spinning sectors are 
women. The activities of the Board for development of coir industries, inter -alia, include 
undertaking scientific, technological and economic research and development activities; 
developing new products & designs; and marketing  of coir and coir products in India and 
abroad.  It also promotes co -operatives  organizations among producers of husks, coir fiber, 
coir yarn and manufacturers of coir products; ensuring remunerative returns to producers and 
manufactures, etc.  The Board has promoted two research for undertaking research activities 
on different aspects of coir industry, which is one of the major agro based rural industries in 
the country.

150. National Small Industries Corporation, established in 1955, has been working with its 
mission of promoting, aiding an d fostering the growth of micro, small and medium 
enterprises.  It has been working to promote the interest of micro, small and medi um 
enterprises and to enhance their competitiveness by providing integrated support services 
under Marketing, Technology, Credit and Support services.

151. The C orporation has been introducing several new schemes from time to time for 
meeting the change aspirations of the micro, small & medium enterprises.  The main objective 
of these schemes is to promote the interest of the micro, small & medium enterprises (MSME) 
and to put them in competitive and advantageous positions.  The schemes of NSIC have been 
found to be very useful in stimulating the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises in 
the country.  
  
152. The Committee appreciates that t o make regular and timely availability of the raw 
materials to MSME’s for their smooth operations, NSIC has made arrangements with the bulk 
manufactures for providing raw materials to the MSMEs at competitive rates.  In case the 
MSME un it needs any credit support, NSIC provides financial assistance for raw material 
procurement by making the payment to suppliers. Any unit seeking this facility may approach 
to any office of the Corporation and submit its application in the prescribed forma t. The 
branch office after evaluating the proposal of unit sanctions the limit to the unit. The unit is 
required to provide a Bank Guarantee of the sanctioned value to NSIC to start availing the 
Raw Material Assistance on credit. 
                 
153.     The manufacturers of aluminum conductors has availed the highest credit facility and 
wax product manufacturing sector has taken the lowest credit facility under our Raw Material 
Assistance Scheme during the current financial year.  
 
154. NSIC has been impl ementing two schemes on behalf of the Government. These two 
schemes are Performance & Credit Rating Scheme & Marketing Assistance Scheme.  
 
Performance & Credit Rating Scheme: NSIC has been implementing “Performance & 
Credit Rating Scheme” for micro and small enterprises (MSEs) on behalf of the Government. 
The scheme is being operated through 06 accredited rating agencies i.e. CRISIL, SMERA, 
ONICRA, CARE, FITCH and ICRA. The Scheme is aimed to create awareness amongst 
micro & small enterprises about the strengths and weakness of their existing operations and to 
provide them an opportunity to enhance their organizational strengths and credit worthiness. 
The rating under the scheme serves as a trusted third party opinion on the capabilities and 
creditworthiness of the micro & small enterprises. An independent rating by an accredited 
rating agency has a good acceptance from the Banks/Financial Institutions, Customers/Buyers 
and Vendors. Under this Scheme, rating fee to be paid by the micro & small enterprises is  
subsidized for the first year only and that is subject to maximum of 75% of the fee or Rs. 
40000/-, whichever is less.  During the year 2008-09, Rs. 7.15 crore was released to NSIC for 
meeting the expenditure under Performance & Credit Rating Scheme. As t he scheme has 
been getting good response from micro & small enterprises, during the year 2008 -09 rating 
was assigned to 5011 units which has resulted into deficit of Rs. 11.71 crore as on 31.3.2009. 
In the year 2009 -10, approx 7500 units would be rated und er the scheme. Hence, the 
budgetary provision in RE 2009 -10 has been increased from Rs. 20.90 crore to Rs. 40.00 
crore, which includes Rs.3.27    Crore for the sub-plans( NER, SCSP, TSP). As this scheme is 
demand driven and proposals from the MSEs of sub -plan categories have not been received 
for rating under the scheme, Rs. 3.18 crore has been surrendered.  
 
Marketing Assistance Scheme:   The main objectives of Marketing Assistance Scheme are to 
enhance the marketing competitiveness of the micro & small ent erprises, to provide them a 
platform for interaction with the individual / institutional buyers, to update them with 
prevalent market scenario and to provide them a forum for redressing their problems. NSIC 
acts as a facilitator to promote marketing effort s and enhance the competency of the micro & 


 38 
small enterprises for capturing the new market opportunities by way of organizing / 
participating in various domestic & international exhibitions/trade fairs, buyers -seller meets, 
intensive campaigns/seminars and other marketing promotion activities.  
 
  155.  NSIC helps micro and small enterprises to participate in International/national 
exhibitions/trade fairs at the subsidized rates to exhibit and market their products. 
Participation in the marketing events pro vides micro & small enterprises an exposure to the 
national/international markets. Bulk and departmental buyers are invited to participate in 
buyer-seller meets to bring them closer to the small enterprises for enhancing their marketing 
competitiveness. Th ese programmes are aimed at vendor developments from small 
enterprises for the bulk manufactures. Intensive campaigns and other marketing events are 
organized all over the country to disseminate/ propagate about the various schemes for the 
benefit of the m icro & small enterprises and  to enrich their knowledge  w.r.t. the latest 
developments, quality standards etc.
