49. The Committee has noted  that the Coir Board is running a beneficial scheme 
Mahila Coir Yojna for self employment of  women.  The Committee during its study 
visit at Lakshadweep visited one of the centres under this Scheme and interacted 
with few spinners and was dismayed over th e stipend given to the women spinners 
which was very insufficient and recommends that the present limit of stipend should 
be raised in view of the increased cost of living and inflation. 

  
 
  Placed below is a catalogue of points which emerged during the 
interactions of the Committee with the representatives of the MSME association:   
(i) Provision for the rehabilitation of sick units as  large number of units are 
becoming sick;  
 
(ii) Appellate Authority where the proble ms of individual sick industry may 
be heard or targets should be fixed for banks that they will have to 
rehabilitate about 20% sick industries; 
  
(iii)  Discrimination between Small and larg e industries as the large industries 
get protection from the Government under BIFR after erosion of 50% or 
more of their net-worth but such protection is not available to sick MSEs; 
 
(iv) Venture Fund of Rs.5000 crore should also be available to Micro 
Enterprises and not only to Medium and Small Enterprise; 
  
(v) Enhancement of  the limit for MSME s for Plant and Machinery from 10 
crore to 25 crore so as to enable the MSMEs to modernize themselves; 
  
(vi) Limit of tax audit should be increased from Rs.60 lakh to Rs.1 crore; 
 
(vii) Increasing  the limit of  excise duty and service tax; 
 
(viii) Enhancement of Marketing sup port under Marketing Development 
Assistance Programme and creation of Export Development Fund; 
 
(ix) Common Application Form for credit/ loan; 
 
(x) Requirement of collateral security; 
 
(xi) Tax exemption  to SMEs which have separate funds for R&D ; 
 
(xii) Enhancement of the limit from 90 days to 6 months for NPA; 
 
(xiii) Enhancement of term loan from 7 years to 15 years at par with the housing 
sector; 
  
50. The Committee draws the attention of the MSME Ministry to the 
aforementioned suggestions and recommends appropriate measures to take up these 
points.  The Committee also would  like to get a detailed note in this regard.   
   
********** 

  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE-AT A GLANCE 
 
 
 
  The Committee strongly feels that a critical and strategic sector like the 
MSME  deserves higher allocation of f unds from the Planning Commission.  The 
Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh while presenting the National Awards to 
Micro, Small and Medium Ent erprises on 28 August 2009,  reiterated Governments' 
commitment to “support, nurse and encour age this very important segment and 
sector of our economy".  The sharp curt ailment of the proposals of the MSME 
Ministry by the Planning Commission is no t in consonance with the vision of the 
Prime Minister to “support, nurse and enco urage this very important segment and 
sector of our economy”.  When the country glowingly acknowledges the vital role of 
MSME sector to increase productivit y, enhance exports, create employment 
opportunities, develop skills of our youth  and promote inclusive growth, it is 
important to give substantially higher allocation to the MSME Ministry.  
(Para No. 9)     
  The Committee feels that allocation of inadequate funds for the MSME 
Ministry is an indication of the mind set of the conc erned organizations of the 
Government which is more aligned to the co rporate sector than the MSME sector.  
Given the importance of the MSME sector for our economy, the Committee strongly 
recommends for the change of such mind set on the part of the   Planning 
Commission and the Ministry of Finance for strengthening the MSME Ministry and 
the MSME sector.   
(Para No. 10) 

  
   
 
The Committee demands an explanation fr om the Ministry to enable it to 
understand the real reasons behind such shortfall.                                   (Para No. 12) 
   The Committee fails to understand the reasons behind non-utilisation of 
funds.  It is important that the Ministry  must use the money allocated to it for 
meeting its targets.  The Committee woul d like to get an explanation from the 
Ministry in this regard.                                                                                (Para No. 14) 
 16. The Committee feels that the scheme s discontinued could have been 
implemented initially on a pilot basis. It is rather deplorable that adequate planning 
was not made to start such schemes which sounded quite good.  The Committee feels 
that the plans must be devised by the Minist ry by taking into account its Vision and 
Mission which have been so eloquently ou tlined by the Ministry.                              
(Para No. 16) 
  The Committee strongly recommends that more money must be allocated for 
establishment of tool rooms across the country.  It is understood that the MSME 
Ministry is also approaching the concerned  organizations within the Government to 
get loans from the International Financial Institutions.  If the Planning Commission 
and the Finance Ministry cannot alloca te more funds for this purpose, then 
necessary permission to the MSME Ministry to get access to bo rrowings from other 
International Banks may be given without any delay.  However, it is strongly 
recommended that we must use our own res ources for this cause which is good for 
the youth of our country and the MSME sector.                                       (Para No. 19)   
 People are queuing up to get facilities under PMEGP ,but the Committee 
finds that the money allocated to subsidiz ed the margin money has not been fully 
utilized.  The Ministry of MSME must expl ain the reasons behind non-utilisation of 
the money.  
(Para No. 22) 

  
  The Committee is happy to note that the allocation for this programme is 
increasing on a year to year basis.  However, it notes that this increase is not in 
proportion to the demand from the youth of our country for setting up of  projects 
under PMEGP.  Taking into account th e increase in budgetary allocation, the 
Committee strongly recommends that the cei ling limits for the projects which are 
beings set up under this programme must be enhanced.  In this context, it 
recommends that while ceiling limit for the manufacturing sector must be increased 
from Rs.25 to Rs.50 lakhs, such limits in case  of service sector may be increase from 
Rs.10 to Rs.15 lakhs.  The Co mmittee is satisfied to note  that projects under the 
PMEGP are being electronically monitored right from the application stage to the 
establishment of the unit.  This online tracking system has enabled the 
implementing agency to ensure transparen cy and accountability.  The Committee 
also observes with satisfaction that th ose beneficiaries under the PMEGP who have 
been trained and passed out from National  Small Industries Corporation, National 
Institute for Entrepreneurs and Small Business Development and MSME 
Development Institute would be exempt ed from undergoing entrepreneur 
development programme under PMEGP.                                                 
 (Para No. 25) 
 
  The Committee regrets that even the public sector banks have failed to reach 
out to the micro sector by providing adequa te credit to it.  Th is is an alarming 
phenomenon which would lead to stunted  and arrested growth of the micro 
enterprises.  The Committee strongly recomm ends that the Reserve Bank of India 
and the Ministry of MSME must monitor th e credit being issued to the micro sector 
and take measures to increase the volume of credit to this sector.          
 (Para No. 26) 
 
  The Committee strongly recommends that policies must be  adopted whereby 
the MSMEs showing good performance would get  enhanced credit automatically.   
(Para No. 27) 
  The Committee appreciated this su ggestion which would promote the 
synergy between the large and small scale industries and feels that  such synergy 

  
would actually promote research and deve lopment capabilities of the MSMEs and 
encourage innovation. The Committee strongly recommends for measures for 
establishing synergy between the large industries and MSME sector. 
(Para No. 28) 
  
  The Committee has noticed that during  the year 2005-06 KVIC was allocated 
total plan budget of Rs.400-500 crores.  Now keeping in view the need as well 
requirement and potential the KVIC  the pl an budget allocation has been increased 
by the Government to the tune of  1565.54 crores in the year 2012-13.  The 
Committee feels that sufficient and sk illed manpower is key to successful 
implementation of the Schemes and Program mes. KVIC has accepted the challenge 
with its present manpower but the work ha s also increased manifold and KVIC has 
to come to the expectation of the Government .  In view of this it seems difficult to 
cope up the work pressure with existing staff strength.  It therefore, recommends 
that the number of officers and staff should also be increased in KVIC in proportion 
to the  budget allocated to achieve the targets and utilize the budget to the full 
extent. 
(Para No. 30) 
  The Committee is of the view that in  changing Indian scenario of high 
growth of the economy and stiff competition from the corporate giants, training 
system in KVIC needs impr ovement through development of appropriate courses, 
introduction of new courses, improveme nt in infrastructure equipment and 
adoption of improved technology and training of trainers.  
 (Para No. 31) 
 
   
  The Committee notes that the reduction of the funds for the Khadi sector is a 
matter of serious concern.  In the aforem entioned paras, the Committee has taken 
note of the fact that the banks have not been issuing adequate credit to the micro 
sector.  As per the above table, the funds coming from the Government to the Khadi 
sector which is part of the small and micro enterprises are also declining.  The 
Committee demands an explanation from the Ministry in this regard.  It is well 

  
known that some of the poorest of the poor weavers and artisans are associated with 
this sector.  The Khadi & Village Industrie s embody the vision of the Father of our 
Nation Mahatma Gandhi.  Any neglect shown to this sector is a neglect of that lofty 
vision.  The Committee finds it unacceptabl e that the Khadi sector is getting such 
treatment from both the Ministry of Fina nce and the Planning Commission.   The 
Committee strongly recommends that remedia l measures must be taken to ensure 
fair allocation of funds to the Khadi componenet of the Khadi & Village Industries.  
(Para No. 33) 
 
  The Committee is of the opinion that the MSME Ministry has fallen short of 
the target.  At a time when skill de velopment is being emphasized by the 
Government and the Ministry is one of th e key nodal Ministries for developing the 
skill of the youth, it is sad to note that it  has not been able to meet the target.  The 
Committee strongly recommends for measures to achieve the target in this respect.   
(Para No. 36) 
   The Committee feels that the establishmen t of six Central Sliver Plants are not 
adequate.  It recommends that the Governme nt should consider for  opening of new 
godowns in each state for ensuring uninterrupted supply of raw material.     
(Para No. 37)   
 
  The Committee in its Report on C redit Facility to MSME Sector had 
recommended that SIDBI should function under the jurisdiction of the MSME 
Ministry.  The Committee reiterates this rec ommendation for better flow of credit 
to the MSME sector.  Accordingly steps must be taken by the Government (Ministry 
of Finance) to bring the SIDBI within the jurisdiction of the MSME Minstry.  
(Para No. 38) 
  The Committee takes into account  the suggestions of some of the 
representatives of the MSME associatio n for opening up a window or a cell for 
MSME to avail of the Extern al Commercial Borrowing.  It recommends that this 
suggestion may be actively considered for its final implementation.   
 (Para No. 39) 

  
    The Committee therefore recommends the Government to consider enhancing the 
allocation for providing assistance fo r setting up of marketing complexes, 
exclusively for KVIC products not only in metro cities but also in state capitals. 
(Para No. 40) 
  As far as the north eastern part of our country is concerned, there is a 
persistent feeling that implementation of the programmes as per the industrial 
policy formulated for that area are not at all satisfactory.  Even the incentives in 
terms of income tax exemption, excise exem ption, etc., have been greatly diluted.  
The Committee urges the Ministry of MSME to take stock of the situation and chalk 
out a programme to address the problem.  
(Para No. 41) 
 
 The Committee agrees with idea of th e some representatives of the MSME 
association that those special economic zo nes which are not being utilized may be 
declared a MSME zone and MSME units may be established on a PPP mode.  
 (Para No. 42)  
 
  The Committee has taken note of the fact that the MSMEs do not have a 
level playing field with the other larg e corporate sectors.  Even the common 
complaint is that the tax rates are skewed in favour of the imported items.  As a 
result, they find it difficult to compete with the industries which import goods from 
the foreign countries.  This is a suggestion which deserves serious and focused 
attention.  The Committee would like to get a detailed explanation on this issue.   
 (Para No. 43) 
 
  The Committee takes note of the fact that the Coir Board has been allocated 
Rs.7.00 crore under Plan (Science & Technology) .   It feels that the amount is 
insufficient in the context of  the vast area of operation of the Board covering the 
coastal belt of the Country which incl udes Lakshadweep and A&N Islands.  The 
Committee feels that appropri ate technology needs to be transferred to the Coir 
Industry.   It entails incubator training  programmes and provision of one time 
assistance upto 50% of the funds needed to establish pilot units.   
(Para No. 44) 

  
  
 
       The Committee therefore rec ommends that it should be modified to provide 
better financial assistance keeping in view the cost of Plant and Machinery.  It also 
recommends that the limit may be extended to Rs.10 lakh from Rs.6 lakhs to benefit 
the coir industry.  
(Para No. 46) 
  The Committee feels that to increase the sale of the coir products, it is 
important to expand the sales network all over India.  
(Para No. 47) 
  The Committee appreciates the overall working of the Coir Board in export 
promotion and recommends timely and hass le free approval of the Government to 
the participants in Trade Fair/Exhibitions.   
(Para No. 48) 
 
  The Committee has noted  that the Coir  Board is running a beneficial scheme 
Mahila Coir Yojna for self employment of  women.  The Committee during its study 
visit at Lakshadweep visited one of the centres under this Scheme and interacted 
with few spinners and was dismayed over th e stipend given to the women spinners 
which was very insufficient and recommends that the present limit of stipend should 
be raised in view of the increased cost of living and inflation. 
(Para No. 49) 
.  
 
  The Committee draws the attentio n of the MSME Ministry to the 
aforementioned suggestions and recommends appropriate measures to take up these 
points.  The Committee also would  like to get a detailed note in this regard.   
  (Para No. 50)

Para-29 
 
Action Taken Note  
 In the CSR Guidelines for Central Public Sector En terprises (CPSEs) issued by 
Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) in April, 2010, it is clearly mentioned that  

5 
 
investment in CSR should be project based.  In view  of this, any activity undertaken for 
promotion of sports and games should be project bas ed. The Committee has rightly 
observed that CPSEs should not divert money meant f or CSR activity for programmes 
not undertaken under the project mode. 
 
 
 
Recommendations/observations  
 The Committee also took a serious note of this iss ue and observed that the 
Department of Public Enterprises Should issue some clarificatory guidelines to all CPSEs 
which will enlighten them as to how the funds under CSR should be spent. 
Para-30 
 
Action Taken Note  
 The CSR guidelines issued by DPE in April, 2010 ha ve specified clearly how the 
funds under CSR should be spent by the CPSEs.  Furt her, the DPE regularly organizes 
workshops and meetings of CPSE representatives with  the MoU Task Force Member for 
stressing again and again the provisions contained in the Guidelines and for removing 
doubts, if any, in implementation of the CSR projects. 
 
 
Recommendations/observations  
 The Committee observes that the MoU system which i nitially focused attention 
on accountability and autonomy of PSEs eventually s tressed on their performance 
appraisal.  The Department of Public Enterprises ma intained that a lot more has to be 
done by PSEs to stress on both financial and non-fi nancial parameters.  The Committee 
welcomes the measures taken by DPE to make MoU syst em more broad based by 
including three Ps which in expanded form means profit, people and planet.                        
Para-31 
 
Action Taken Note  
 DPE has issued comprehensive guidelines on CSR, R& D and Sustainable 
Development. These are mandatory elements of MoU for CPSEs and specific weights are 
assigned to these in MoU. These initiatives have be en well accepted by CPSEs in the 
MoUs signed for the year 2012-13. By introducing th ese recent measures, MoU has 
become broad-based forward looking. 
 
 
 

6 
 
Recommendations/observations  
 It is the age when the business enterprises have t o be run on the basis of modern 
principles which are different from the norms gover ning Government departments.  
Therefore, the Committee feels that the MoU system should be such which would enable 
the PSEs and its management to take advantage of th e opportunities that are now 
available in the market for maximizing their profits.  While doing so, the PSEs concerned 
must avoid the problems and threats which might pose danger to its commercial viability.  
The non-financial parameters in the MoU are often d escribed as soft bellies.  It is 
important, therefore, to give adequate weightage to  both financial and non-financial 
parameters .                                 
  Para-32 
Action Taken Note  
 In the MoU Guidelines for the year 2012-13, the fi nancial and non-financial 
parameters have weightage of 50% equally with an exception for Sick & loss making and 
Section 25 companies where the ratio is 40:60. 
 
 The non-financial parameter is based on the princi ples of Specific, measurable, 
attainable, result oriented & Tangible (SMART) and includes Dynamic Parameters, 
Sector-specific& Enterprise-specific Parameters, Co rporate Social Responsibility (CSR), 
Research & Development (R&D), Sustainable Developme nt (SD), Human Resource 
Management (HRM) and Compliance of Corporate Governance (CG).   
 
 
Recommendations/observations  
 The time has now come for the corporation bodies n ot only to use their strategic 
assets but also take advantage of the opportunities  available on a pro active basis.  A laid 
back approach will not help in furthering the cause  of business. The Committee, 
therefore, feels that MoU system must go beyond fin ancial performance and give 
importance to the issue of productivity improvement.  
  Para-33 
 
Action Taken Note  
 DPE has issued guidelines on the following issues with specific weightages in 
MoU: 
 (a) Adoption of innovative practices (b) Committed  capital Investments (CAPEX) 
by CPSE and (c) Listing of eligible CPSEs. These st rategic issues will go a long way in 
enhancing productivity of CPSEs.

INTRODUCTION 
  
  
 I, the Chairman of the Department-re lated Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Industry, having been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred 
and Thirty –Seventh Report on the Revival an d Restructuring of Hotel Corporation of 
India Ltd. pertaining to Ministry of Civil Aviation. 
 
 
2. The Committee held detailed discu ssion with the Management of Hotel 
Corporation of India Ltd and received inputs for this Report.   
 
 
3. I, thank the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Department of Public Enterprises for 
furnishing the valuable inputs during the meetings.  
 
 
4. The Committee in its meeting held on 30
th August, 2012 considered and adopted 
the report. 
 
  
 
 
 
  
Tiruchi Siva 
Chairman                              
                          Department -related Parliamentary 
                                                                                       Standing Committee   on   Industry 
 
 
 
New Delhi 
August, 2012 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(ii) 
 
 
 
 

  
 
 
REPORT  
 
 The hospitality sector in India of which the hotel industry is a crucial component 
is growing and expanding with the growth a nd expansion of tourism, travel industry and 
above all economy. It is in this context that the Committee as part of its exercise to study 
the MOU performance of the public sector enterprises decided to apply its mind to 
analyze the MOU performance of the Hotel Corporation of India Limited (HCIL). 
2. The narrative of the report is of course ba sed on the threadbare and deep analysis 
of the material supplied to the Committee and the interactions with the officials of the Air 
India and HCIL. But the Committee’s understa ting went beyond this academic exercise 
and actually flowed from  the first hand experience of its Members  staying in the 
Centaur Hotel, Sri Nagar, owned  by the HCIL, and understanding the problems and 
challenges which the Hotel and its management and employees confronted. 
3. The genesis of the HCIL is traced to July 8, 1971 when it was set up by the Air 
India as a public limited company under the Companies Act, 1956. The world over, the 
air lines during that time had developed the tradition and practice of entering into the 
hotel industry. It had become a dominant intern ational practice for the air lines to expand 
their frontier by stepping into the hospitali ty sector. The Air I ndia was no exception to 
that prevailing trend. Being the national carri er with monopoly in the aviation sector it 
ventured into the hotel industry with the twin objectives of promoting tourism and 
catering. The motive force was to serve the passengers by providing better products and 
services not only at the international air ports but also at other places of tourist interest. 

  
4. Accordingly two hotels bearing the co mmon brand name of Centaur and two 
Flight Kitchens bearing the brand name of Chefair were set up by the HCI. While hotels 
are located in Delhi and Sri Nagar, the Flight Kitchens are situated in Mumbai and Delhi. 
As on March 2012 the total number of employees in the rolls of the Corporation stood at 
1658 out of which 1340 fall into the permanent category and 318 belong to 
temporary/contractual/casualcategory.  
Centaur Hotel, Delhi: 
5. The establishment and functioning of the Ce ntaur Hotel, Delhi, dates back to 1982 
when the Asian Games were organised in th e city. It has got 376 rooms and is located 
close to the Indira Gandhi International Ai r Port. The Committee is given to understand 
that the Hotel could never utilise its full pot ential in spite of so many positive factors 
which include its advantageous location clos e to a major air port of our country. The 
major reason cited for the failure of the Hote l to attract business is  lack of renovation. It 
is rather sad that the capacity utilisation of the Hotel is only 64 per cent. It is worth 
reproducing from the brief submitted by the HC I to the Committee. It states "In the 
absence of proper renovation of  the guest rooms, restaurant s, kitchen and public areas, 
the Hotel could not attract business and is  presently working on approximately 64 per 
cent of its capacity." The underutilization of  the capacity is reflected in poor MOU 
performance of the HCI.  
6. One of the defining features of the hos pitality sector, part icularly the hotel 
industry is renewal and creativity on a continuous basis. Without adopting measures to  
 

  
renew and renovate any hotel in the buoyant hosp itality sector is bound to be left behind 
and might even perish. Since the organi sation of the Asian Games in 1982 and the 
liberalization of Indian economy later, the prospects of tourism and hotel industry got 
brightened and the demand pattern for hotel  rooms in all segments of hotel chain 
witnessed significant rise. It is rather sad to note that when the demand for hotels in India 
was rising the business of the Centaur Hotel in Delhi was declining due to lack of 
renovation. With its building and facilities having not undergone any serious renovation 
and upgradation, it is not surprising that th e hotel is no more in reckoning in the 
hospitality sector and, theref ore, not a preferred destina tion for the valued customers 
neither from within India nor from abroad.  It is appropriately obs erved that "ITDC and 
HCI boast of some of the major locations in major cities but are relatively under 
performers, as compared with their private sector counter parts." 
7. However, the officials of the HCI presented before the Committee  hopeful 
picture of the Hotel by referri ng to the outcome budget 2012-13 of the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation where Rs.11 crores has been a llocated for renovation of the hotel and 
upgradation of equipments. The brief submitted to the Committee also mentions that 
there is hope and expectation that the pa rent company the Air India would provide 
business support to the hotel. The brief supplie d to the Committee also states that the  
Centaur Hotel, Delhi, “…has also come into the expansion plan of Terminal-3” which, it 
is hoped, would benefit the Hotel. Howeve r, the Committee while taking note of such 
hopeful signs observes that no final decision has been taken in this regard.  
8. While analyzing the high expectation of the Centaur Hotel, Delhi, to get business 
from the Air India the Committee is mindful of  the fact that the parent body is itself in 

  
red and even not signing the MOU even after the direction of the Cabinet Secretary to do 
so. There is a plan being drawn up to provide  100 rooms in the Centaur Hotel, Delhi for 
use by Air India for the operation of their back offices.  The Committee was informed 
that the implementation of this plan “… will  benefit both the organi zations in terms of 
Air India acquiring space at a lower rent near the airport and the Hotel getting round the 
year business”.   
9. The Committee notes that the Government  of India has decided to pump in Rs.20, 
000 crores to revive Air India.  It generate s hope that some funds  from the corpus of 
money released by the Government for the national carrier might be allocated for the HCI 
for boosting up its financial hea lth and restoring the commerci al viability of the hotels 
which are being operated by the HCI. The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends for substantial allocation of resources made available to the Air India 
for making the units working under the HCI more financially viable and sound. The 
amount so released must be in addition to Rs. 11 crore earmarked in the outcome 
budget for renovation and upgradation of the Centaur Hotel, Delhi.  
Centaur Lake View Hotel, Srinagar: 
10. The hotel with 249 rooms commenced its operations in 1984 a nd is located not 
only in the prime land but also in the picturesque surroundings of Dal lake with majestic 
hills in the horizon providing a rare and scenic backdrop. The land and magnificent 
surroundings adds immense inta ngible value to the hotel and it would be a highly 
preferred destination for any tourist visiting Kashmir which is justly described as the 
paradise on earth. In fact, it would be a dream for any tourist to stay is such a 
surrounding. The Committee stayed in this hotel and had understood the problems not 

  
just theoretically but practically by experiencing the difficulties an d facing the odds with 
some degree of empathy and understanding.  The rooms are spacious and the gadgets 
fixed there are so archaic and faulty that  no guest would decide to spend money for 
availing of such substandard facilities. It is  evident from the average occupancy of the 
hotel which stands at 108 rooms per day.  
11. In peeping into its history the Co mmittee found that the hotel, after its 
establishment in 1984,  did not get any busine ss worth the name as the state of Jammu 
and Kashmir faced turmoil and disturbance for almost two decades arising out of 
terrorism and terrorist related violence. It was informed that no steps were taken to 
renovate the hotel due to such intractable pr oblems. In face of a hopeless situation of 
lawlessness the hotel sustained itself w ith meager business provided by certain 
Government agencies.   
12. Taking into account the low business turn out, the Government of India 
contemplated to hand over the property to the State Government. However, a final call on 
this matter is yet to be made. Notwithstanding the organizational issues, there appears to 
be a positive aspect for CLVH, Srinagar, as Kashmir valley has once again begun to 
attract tourists from across the world as tensions seems to have alleviated. Timely up-
gradation of the facilities by utilizing Rs.5crore which has b een allocated in the outcome 
budget of the Ministry for  the year 2012-13 would definitely help the hotel to cash in on 
this spurt in tourism and shore up its fortune. The Committee notes that the HCI is 
confident that the hotel would be able to manage itself financially and make profit by 
utilizing the amount earmarked in the outcome budget.  
 

  
13. However, the hopeful note of the HCI and its positive feeling of turning around 
the Centaur Hotel in Sri Nagar has to be appr eciated in the context of certain hard facts 
vis-à-vis the maintenance of the hotel rooms. The average expenditure on maintenance of 
hotel room per day is Rs53/ per day. The av erage income per room per day is Rs.2823/ 
per day. Incidentally 55 rooms are occupied by the office of the Accountant General with 
per day room rent of Rs.1200.  
 
14. During the interactions with the Memb ers of the Committee it was informed by 
the hotel officials that the average age of th e employees of the Centaur Hotel, Srinagar, 
ranges from 52 to 54 years. With such high age profile of the staff th e hotel is not in a 
position to put up a good show which can be done by a smart set of employees ready to 
put the best foot forward. The non-recruitmen t of the staff for several decades due to 
persistence of disturbance in the State has proved to be a drag on the future progress of 
the hotel. It is sad that no effort has been taken to place a proper plan  to recruit young 
people to manage the affairs of the hotel.  
 
15. The Committee reiterates that more f unds out of the corpus earmarked for 
the Air India may be used for renovation and upgradation of the facilities of the 
Centaur Hotel in Sri Nagar.  
 
16. The Committee also came to know that many of the rooms of the hotel in Sri 
Nagar have been occupied by the security forces and other officials. In the changed 
scenario marked by improved law and order si tuation and greater fl ow of tourists to 
Jammu and Kashmir, it is important to make a ll the rooms available to the tourists. In the 
peak tourist season it is almost impossible to  get a room in the Kashmir valley. It is 

  
against this backdrop that urgent measures must be taken to vacate the rooms occupied by 
the security officials so as to   make them available rising number of tourists.  
 
17. The Committee notes that on  earlier years th e money allocated to the hotels run 
by the HCI was not fully utilized. For instance out of the Rs.15 crores allocated to each of 
the hotels located in Delhi and Kashmir fo r the year 2011-11 and 2011-12 only slightly 
more than 10 per cent were utilized. It is rather shocking that money allocated are not 
being fully utilized by HCI which is defici ent in cash and because of which its hotel 
infrastructure is much below the bench mark seen in the expanding hospitality  sector.  
 
18. Earlier it has been mentioned that th e HCIL apart from operating two Centaur 
Hotels is engaged in running two flight kitchens known as Chefair each one of which is 
located in Mumbai and Delhi.     
 
19. Chefair Flight Catering Delhi: Commissi oned in 1986 its capaci ty utilization is 
only 22 per cent.  This pathetic performance of the unit is attributed to lack of renovation 
of its kitchen infrastructure.  Initially th e capacity utilization ranged from 35 to 40 per 
cent due to depreciation and normal wear an d tear of the equipments installed.  The 
Committee takes note of the fact that rupees  six crores have been allocated in the 
outcome budget 2012-13 of the Ministry for renovation and restoratio n of the facilities 
available for flight kitchen.   
 
20. Chefair Flight Catering Mumbai: The unit which started functioning in 1986 is 
able to utilize 32 per cent of its installe d capacity.  The same problem of lack of 
renovation which plagued the Centaur Hotels in the Chefair Flight Catering Delhi is 
plaguing the Chefair Flight  Catering Mumbai.  Its problems have been further 

  
compounded because of the bifurcation of the catering contract by the Air India.  As a 
result, this unit only caters to a few flight s which is far below the target.  The Committee 
was informed that the area where the Chef air unit of Mumbai was operating was taken 
away for expanding the airport.  As a result , the Chefair was shifted and relocated.  The 
Committee understood that the HCI is insisting for a fully deve loped infrastructure in the 
vicinity of the airport to run the flight kitc hen.  The Committee takes note of the fact that 
work for this purpose is in progress.  The Committee also takes note of the fact that 
rupees three crore has been allocated in the outcome Budget for the year 2012-13 of the 
Ministry for the renovation of the flight kitchen in Mumbai.  The HCI maintains that with 
the new infrastructure to be made available to the flight kitchen in Mumbai and with the 
new budgetary provision for its renovation a nd upgradation the flight  kitchen would get 
adequate business not only from Air India but also from other airlines.  The turn around 
plan proposals for the 12
th Plan period states that Chefai r Delhi and Chefair Mumbai are 
expected to commence operations of Air India lounges at Terminal 3 Delhi (both 
domestic and internatio nal) and Air India Maharaja Lounge  at Terminal 2C at Mumbai 
respectively to fulfill the requirements of Air India.   
 
21. Earlier the capacity utilizat ion of both the flight kitc hens in Delhi and Mumbai 
have been discussed.  It may be reiterated that while the Chefair Delhi is operating with 
22 per cent of the installed capacity the Chef air Mumbai is operating with only 32 per 
cent.  When the Committee wanted to know  how many meals per day are being supplied 
to Air India by Chefair of Delhi and Mumbai  it was informed that only 4300 meals are 
supplied as against the requirement of 23000 meals (13000 meals from Delhi and 10000 
meals from Mumbai per day).   
 

  
22. The Committee notes that the HCIL did not  take any measure for renovation of its 
hotel infrastructure and flight  kitchens due to paucity of funds.  Such gross neglect for 
renewal and restoration of the facilities at its disposal has caused  serious problems at a 
time when the hotel and hospitality sector is  expanding in geometric proportions.  When 
tourism sector is getting renewed attention due to its vast potential and when  the 
Government is launching a campaign called ‘Ati thi Devo Bhavah’ to attract both foreign 
and domestic tourists to visit different parts of our country, it is important for the HCIL to 
be part of this campaign and build up its cap acity by constantly renova ting its facilities.  
As stated earlier, the Committee would like to  see the Air India, the parent body of the 
HCIL, take measures so that at least some por tion of amount is released for its revival is 
utilized for HCIL. It will help the HCIL  to improve its MoU performance. The 
Committee recommends that this amount must  be at least Rs.100 crore which would be 
exclusive of Rs. 25crores already earmarked in the outcome budgets as mentioned in the 
earlier paragraphs. The involvement, dedi cation and commitment of the employees, 
management and the government are fundame ntal perquisites for the maintenance, 
revival and success of any PSE like Centaur Hotel, Srinagar.  No tangible result would be 
achieved by pumping more money unless the employees and management of the Hotel do 
not qualitatively improve their performance. In addition to the monetary or budgetary 
support there must be innovative and creative planning to revamp the infrastructure of the 
hotels and flight kitchens unde r the HCL and refurbish their image for attracting tourists 
and passengers to its quality products and services.       
  
 
  

  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE-AT A 
GLANCE 
 
   The Committee, therefore, strongly reco mmends for substantial allocation 
of resources made available to the Air India for making the units working under the 
HCI more financially viable and sound. The am ount so released must be in addition 
to Rs. 11 crore earmarked in the outcome budget for renovation and upgradation of 
the Centaur Hotel, Delhi.  
(Para 9) 
 The Committee reiterates that more f unds out of the corpus earmarked for 
the Air India may be used for renovation and upgradation of the facilities of the 
Centaur Hotel in Sri Nagar.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry,
having been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred and Thirty Eighth
Report on Action Taken Notes furnished by the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises
(Department of Heavy Industry) on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two
Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) pertaining to Department
of Heavy Industries.
2. I thank the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises (Department of Heavy
Industry) for furnishing the Action Taken Notes on the recommendations contained in the
Committee’s Two Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report.
3. The Committee in its meeting held on the 19
th March, 2013 considered and adopted the
Report.
TIRUCHI SIV A
NEW D ELHI; Chairman,
19th March, 2013 Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Industry.

1
REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises (Department of Heavy Industry) on the recommendations
contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report on the Demands For Grants
(2012-13) pertaining to Department of Heavy Industry.
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises (Department of Heavy Industry) in respect of the recommendations contained in the
Report. These have been categorized as follows:
Chapter-I– The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations
as mentioned in the Chapter–I of the Report.
Chapter-II – The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to
pursue in view of the Government’s replies.
In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue them for the present.
Chapter-III – The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has
either not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its reply.
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendations
contained in Chapter–III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanations thereof.
Chapter-IV – The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the
Ministry have not been received.
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished the
interim replies or couched its language in vague terms therefore, the Committee desires that the
Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects of recommendations categorized in Chapter-
IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the
Committee.
3. The details of the ATR is being discussed in the succeeding pages.

2
CHAPTER-I
The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry
Recommendations/Observations
1. The Committee notes that the IEBR of some important PSEs under DHI are far from the
expected figures during 2010-11 and 2011-12. It is a matter of grave concern that HPC is still
reeling under the impact of non-availability of raw materials . Though, the Committee has dealt with
the issue separately in one of its earlier reports, it is reiterated that an important enterprise in the
North Eastern Area should not be allowed to incur losses owing to problems which can be sorted
out by approaching the State Government and the Ministry of Railways. (Para 28)
Action Taken
Internal mobilization of resources has lagged behind the expected figures as the market
conditions have not been favourable in recent years. In respect of HPC, the State Government has
already been apprised about the impact of the non-availability of raw materials and their help is
sought for in sorting out the matter. State Government of Assam on its part has already held three
rounds of the meeting to find out the ways and means for improving the raw material scenario.
Regular follow up is being made with Railway authorities both at Guwahati and at New Delhi in
the matter of allotment of rakes for supply of raw material to HPC units, the response to which
is positive.
Committee’s observation
The Committee does not accept the DHI’s argument attributing failure to mobilize
even the conservative estimates of Internal and Extra Budgetary Resources (IEBR), on
market conditions. There exists huge scope in the infrastructure sector. The argument of
adverse market conditions must be used carefully and efforts should be made to overcome
such trend. The Committee also noted that the BE (2010-11) for IEBR were retained even
in RE (2010-11). Yet actual figures were way below the RE (2010-11). The Committee would
like to know the actual IEBR for 2011-12. The Committee also notes that PSU’s capacity of
generating IEBR is decreasing every year.

CHAPTER-II
The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does
not desire to pursue in view of the Government's replies
Recommendations/Observations
1. The Committee finds that the Plan funds allocated for 2011-12 have been well utilized by
DHI. It is the lower rate of utilization of Non-Plan funds that has pulled down the overall utilization
figure for the year. In this circumstance, the Committee views the spurt in Plan allocation for
2012-13 to be encouraging and observes that the Department should be able to continue the
efficient utilization of funds during the current year also. This will go a long in augmenting the
performance of CPSEs under DHI and the schemes of the Department. (Para 4)
Action Taken Note
Total allocation of funds for the financial year 2012-13 is Rs. 1009.67 crore, Rs. 553.00
crore under Plan and Rs. 456.67 crore under Non-Plan. Out of Rs. 553.00 crore under Plan,
Rs. 488.48 crore is allocated to National Automotive Testing and Research & Development
Infrastructure Project. All efforts will be made to utilize the entire allocation of funds under Plan
& Non-Plan during the financial year 2012-13.
Committee’s observation
The Committee expects that both the Plan and Non-Plan expenditure are evenly
spread out four quarters of the Financial Year. Cautions must be maintained as per the GFR
56 (3).
Recommendations/Observations

Heavy Industry, as it is one of the largest PSEs in India and has every potential to become an
established global player in its field. While studying the Turnover and PBT of BHEL, the
Committee’s attention was drawn to a decrease in the growth parameters in relation to 2011-12
compared to 2010-11. However, the Committee takes note of the explanations in this regard
provided by the BHEL. Even so, since the Committee views BHEL as a would-be Maharatana
Company in the near future, it is observed that BHEL has to take measures to prevent shortfall in
its performance. (Para 35)

To further enhance the performance, the company is focusing efforts on several thrust
areas which include Capability enhancement, Cost competitiveness, Diversification & Strategic Tie-
ups etc. A brief account of the actions taken in these areas is as following:
(i) The significant actions taken as a part of enhancing cost competitiveness include
(a) maximizing the level of Indigenization of high value items, (b) localization of parts
and components through vendor development, (c) competitive buying by way of
widening vendor base, Rate contracts Memorandum of Understanding with suppliers,
bulking of generic requirements, leveraging Information Technology through Reverse

(ii) As a part of expanding its business vista in non-power area, the company is pursuing
diversification initiatives in Renewables, Transmission and Transportation segments. In

Transmission, the thrust is for Products & Systems for ultrahigh voltage transmission
(765 and 1200 KV), Gas Insulated Substations etc.
Committee’s observation
The Committee notes that BHEL’s capacity of generating IEBR has been decreasing
despite its ambitious expansion plan. The Committee is also cognisant that BHEL’s order
books are impressive, however, there have been persistent complaints about delay in supply
of equipments and in commissioning the projects, thereby causing significant financial
losses to the client companies. The Ministry and the Board of the Company must ensure
that the expansion plan of the Company must also include the measures of timely delivery
of contracts and equipments to the clients.
Recommendations/Observations

The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee
has either not accepted the replies of the Ministry or has asked
the Ministry to review its replies
Recommendations/Observations
1. Notwithstanding the explanation furnished by the Department, the Committee notes with
concern that a project which has immense potential for clean power generation and minimal
environmental impact has been progressing at snails pace since the inking of MoU in the first half
of 2008. The Committee, therefore, recommends that apart from the equity participation of the

highest level possible for the clearance of the funding proposal under clean energy fund.
(Para 19)
Action Taken Note
As per advice of Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee (DRPSC) on

the funding proposal for the IGCC project under Clean Energy Fund. BHEL would also follow up

Further Recommendation
The Committee expects that DHI instead of BHEL should have taken up the issue with
appropriate ministries and the State Government at highest level.

CHAPTER-IV
The Recommendations/observations in respect of which
final replies of the Ministry have not been received
Recommendations/Observations
1. The Committee notes that the Department has been able to secure only 15.68 per cent of
the Plan funds they sought for the year 2012-13. The funds for all major schemes have been
drastically curtailed. The Committee feels that it will be difficult for DHI to implement the schemes
efficiently. Taking into account the efficient utilisation of plan resources by DHI during 2011-12,
the Committee feels that the Department deserves a substantially higher allocation for 2012-13. The
Committee expects that the DHI with its proven record of good work would be able to persuade
and convince the Ministry of Finance to provide more funds at the time when the revised estimates
are finalised. The Committee also strongly recommends for higher allocation of funds for the
Department of Heavy Industry. (Para 6)
Action Taken Note
The suggestion of the Committee has been noted. The plan scheme of the Department for
the Twelfth Five Year Plan have been devised to provide the much needed support to the Machine
tools/Capital Goods Sector, the Automotive Sector and the CPSEs under the Department. Some of
the schemes are in the nature of pre-approved schemes during the previous Plan, which have to
continue in this Plan. Considerable efforts towards modernization, technology up-gradation, revival
of the CPSEs are also integrated in the Plan proposal. Therefore, the proposed allocation is essential
for realization of Plan target and is fully justified. Also efforts will be made to convince the
Planning Commission and Finance Ministry for more funds.
Committee’s observation
The Committee may be informed of the outcome of the Ministry’s efforts with the
Ministry of Finance and the Planning Commission in respect of enhancing the Plan outlay
for the Year 2012-13.
Recommendations/Observations
2. The Committee hopes that a path breaking project like NATRiP which is of great
significance for the automobile sector is completed according to the revised time schedule. It is
sad to note that the project has received only about 45 per cent of the budgetary support sought.
The Committee observes that no stone should be left unturned to complete the project as per the
revised time line of December, 2012. The officials of the DHI informed the Committee that it
would not be possible to complete the project by December, 2012 due to inadequate funds. NATRiP
is a project of national significance and of critical relevance to the automobile sector in India.
Given the fact that India is now emerging as a global hub for the automobile industry, it is
imperative that NATRiP is extended all facilities including the necessary monetary support for its
completion as per the revised schedule. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Finance
and the Planning Commission must be supportive for this project which has been delayed so long
due to insufficient allocation. Therefore, it is strongly recommended that more funds must be
released for this project. (Para 10)

9
Action Taken Note
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in April 2011 approved the revised cost estimate
of Rs. 2288.06 crore, in place of original cost estimate of Rs. 1718 crore due to budget escalation
and revised project completion date of 31.12.2012 from the earlier completion date of 30.09.2011.
NATIS, as on date, has received total funds of Rs. 1170.44 crores out of which
Rs.1150.96 crore has been utilized/committed and the balance amount is expected to be spent
shortly. During 2011-12, against a demand of Rs. 1131.85 crore, only a sum of Rs. 355.38 crore
was allocated. For additional funding during 2011-12, the matter was taken up with Department of
Expenditure, Ministry of Finance as well as Planning Commission. However, the additional fund
requirement was not acceded to. During 2012-13 also, as against the projected demand of
Rs. 1104.62 crore (Rs. 1095.13 crore as budgetary support and Rs. 9.49 crore on account of
internal accruals) only an amount of Rs. 488.48 crore has been allocated for NATRiP. As in
the past, the Department would take adequate steps for procuring additional funds for NATRiP in
2012-13 at the appropriate stage i.e. first supplementary stage as well as with the Ministry of
Finance and Planning Commission, so that insufficient funding does not have an adverse impact on
the schedule of the completion of the project.
Committee’s observation
The Committee takes note that of the total original cost of Rs 1718 crore, so far
only Rs. 1150 could be utilised. Yet the Ministry has been seeking steep rise in annual
allocations. The Committee would like to know the reason for such steep rise in demand.
The Committee is also apprehensive over time and cost overrun. The Committee also notes
that NATRiP was conceived as Public Private Partnership project. Whether efforts have been
made to bridge the resource gap by involving private partners?
Recommendations/Observations
3. The Committee is disheartened to note that the capital goods sector is almost handicapped
due to free flow of imported technology. In fact, import dependence is truly worrisome. The
absence of countervailing duties and elevated export duty structure seem to be adding to the vows
of the sector. In this circumstance, the Committee recommends that the Government may look into
re- imposition of countervailing duties on import of plants and machinery and rationalize the excise
duty structure so that the indigenous industrial units are not put in a disadvantageous position
vis-à-vis the foreign players. Technology transfer should be incentivised and programme initiatives
for R&D, joint technology development and acquisition, etc., should be prioritized . (Para 14)
Action Taken Note
Capital Goods Sector has been opened to import freely. Before 1991, the Sector had some
restriction on import of new machinery as well as second hand. Owing to import restriction the
manufacturers earlier forced to manufacture machinery indigenously. The technology collaborations
as well as joint ventures were happening. The technology was transferred in most of the machinery
sector with imposition of phased manufacturing programme to facilitate indigenous development of
critical components. After 1991, due to liberalization policy import of most capital goods, new as
well as used without any age limit, started to take place without any significant technology transfer.
The indigenous manufacture of machinery dried up slowly except large manufacturers who
managed to market their products. Generally, the manufacturers, particularly SMEs could not buy
the technology because of either non availability or high value of technology transfer. Lack of
desired R&D institutions added to the woes of the SME Sector.

10
In the Capital Goods Sectors, some specified machineries relating to power equipment,
mining & construction equipments and textile machinery are exempted from customs duty. Capital
Goods Industry is a capital and technology intensive Sector with a long gestation period.
Technology transfer is necessary for production of hi-tech and energy efficient contemporary
machinery. Working Group on Capital Goods & Engineering Sector set up by Planning Commission
under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Heavy Industry recommended, several measures to address
the above issues such as establishment of Product Development Centres, Industry Specific Cluster
Parks, Common Facility Centres, Technology Transfer/modernisation/capacity expansion through
Interest Rate Subvention, Research & Development through IITs/NITs as well as through DSIR &
CSIR, Skill Development through Capital Goods Skill Council, Duty and Tax Rationalization through
D/o Revenue and Export promotion through EEPC. Department of Heavy Industry has taken up the
issue of taxation policy reforms with Department of Commerce, Department of Revenue and the
other concerned Ministries. Recently in a Meeting of the Committee of Secretaries, held on
23.5.2012, a decision has been taken to impose certain restrictions on import of Second Hand
Capital Goods. The Department is in touch with the Department of Commerce for implementation
of the CoS decision. The Department has also taken up the issue of R&D support to the Capital
Goods Sector with Scientific Ministries.
Committee’s observation
The Committee may be informed of the steps taken by the Government on the
recommendations of the Working Group on Capital Goods and engineering sector of
Planning Commission. Whether adequate budgetary provisions have been made and whether
any policy been notified in this regard.
Recommendations/Observations
4. The Committee noted that with the economic reforms and liberalisation, technology flow
has come down drastically. It is given to understand that the Planning Commission set up a
Committee headed by Mr. Arun Maira to study the situation. The Report of the Arun Maira
Committee recommended for imposition of customs duty to a certain extent. The Department also
inform the Committee that the Minister for Department of Heavy Industry also took up the matter.
The Department was expecting that there would be some budgetary provision to remedy the
situation. However, the unfavourable situation for the capital goods sector continues to haunt the
entire Indian industry. It is tragic that our capacity to manufacture power plants and other capital
goods equipments are not being harnessed due to a liberal import regime with zero custom duty.
(Para 15)
Action Taken Note
The Committee headed by Shri Arun Maira was in favour of imposition of custom duty on
import of power plant equipment in which indigenous capabilities exist and the Department has
supported this viewpoint. The Government has introduced Zero import duty window to large
sectors like construction sector, power sector, mining project etc. Though domestic manufacturers
are capable to meet the local demand in the case of power equipment, yet they are in a
disadvantageous position vis-a-vis  global players because of zero import duty. Production of
domestic manufacturers is subject to excise and other forms of taxation whereas imported
machinery are free of such tax burdens. This is eroding the domestic competence.
The Department has been advocating on various fora for providing a level playing field to
domestic manufacturers against import of machinery with zero duty. Recently, the Cabinet has

11
approved the proposal to levy 5 per cent custom duty + 12% CVD+ 4% SAD on imported power
equipment, thus settling this long pending issue.
Committee’s observation
The Committee would like to know if such measures will raise the cost of power
production and whether domestic manufactures will be able to cater to growing demands of
power equipments particularly in view of greater private sector participation in power
generation.
Recommendations/Observations
5. Further, the Committee strongly recommends that import of second hand goods should be
discouraged to the extent possible, if not banned. HEC, HMT and other national level companies
have to be promoted for the cause of capital goods sector and bigger companies like BHEL should
be made fountainheads of Capital Goods Exports. A level playing field which would entail imposition
of customs duty on the imported technology and favourable duty structure for the indigenous
industry would promote competitiveness among domestic and foreign players. The scheme
Enhancement of Competitiveness in Capital Good Sector was proposed by the Working Group on
Capital Goods and Engineering Sector set up by the Planning Commission. The Committee feels
that adequate measures must be taken to approve the scheme and implement it during the Twelfth
Five Year Plan. The Committee also recommends that maximum budgetary support must be
provided for this purpose. (Para 16)
Action Taken Note
The Department of Heavy Industry is in agreement with the proposal of restricting import
of second hand capital goods. The Department has been taking up the issue of restriction of import
of second hand capital goods with the concerned Ministries/Departments. The similar view was
taken by the Department in the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) meeting dated 23.05.2012 on the
issue of promotion of domestic capital goods industry which imposed the following restrictions on
import of second hand capital goods:
(a) Import of second hand capital goods may be totally prohibited in schemes with explicit
or implicit subsidy, such as TUFS (Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme), EPCG
(Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme), CLCSS (Credit Linked Capital Subsidy
Scheme).
(b) The second hand capital goods may be valued at 75 per cent of their original value.
This valuation will be for the purpose of determining import duty and not for any other
purpose, unless otherwise specified.
(c) Import of machinery more than five years old may not be allowed unless a different
maximum age is specified by DoC, in consultation with concerned Ministry/
Department and NMCC, keeping in view its sectoral requirement.
(d) NMCC may separately examine the impact of FTAs on domestic industries and
thereafter inter-ministerial consultations on its findings may be undertaken.
(e) NMCC may examine the issue of accurate and reliable data collection in respect of
import of second hand capital goods and suggest a suitable mechanism therefor.
Department is also pursuing with the Planning Commission for approval of a Scheme on
enhancement of competitiveness of the Capital Goods Sector. The consideration of the Scheme,

12
proposed during the Eleventh Plan was deferred to the Twelfth Plan period. The present Scheme
proposed has an outlay of Rs. 2360 crore. The Scheme envisages, inter alia , establishment of
Product Development Centres, Interest rate subvention and Common Facility Centres & Sector
specific parks for Capital Goods Sector. The DHI is also pursuing proposal based support for the
capital goods sector from other Ministries concerning R&D, export promotion, industrial
infrastructural development etc.
Committee’s observation
The Committee would like to know whether the restrictions imposed on the import
of second hand Capital Goods have been accepted by the Government and notified
accordingly. Also, how does DHI propose to proceed on the various other components of the
decision taken by the Committee of Secretaries. Whether NMCC (National Manufacturing
Competitiveness Council) has given its views in this regard and on the impact of FTAs (Free
Trade Agreement) on the domestic industries .
Recommendations/Observations
6. The Committee would like to have detailed explanation in this regard.
(Para 22)
Action Taken Note
A revised proposal for revival of Scooters India Limited (SIL) on its own is under
consideration for obtaining approval of Cabinet. The revised proposal of SIL, prepared on the basis
of joint study undertaken by Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Pune with
M/s Scooters India Limited, Lucknow is for exploring the possibilities of revival of the company
on its own. The company through revised revival proposal addressing all possible key areas
including HR, production and technology is expected to achieve the revival targets for sustainability,
growth and profitability of SIL. Accordingly, a draft Cabinet Note with the approval of Hon’ble
Minister (HI&PE) has been circulated on 16.07.2012 to all the concerned Ministries/Departments
for seeking comments.
Committee’s observation
The Committee would like to know whether Scooters India Limited proposes to revive itself
‘on its own’. Also, whether such revival entails clearing of present liabilities through budgetary
provisions.
Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee views that the allocation and utilization of funds for VRS of CPSEs during
the Eleventh Plan is not satisfactory. Only Instrument Ltd, Kota (ILK) looks to have utilized their
funds completely. Large amounts of funds have been allocated to HPF, BSCL & BBUNL over the
years but their utilization is shown to be ‘nil’, which is not at all encouraging. This scenario either
brings out the lacunae plaguing the implementation of VRS. (Para 24)
Action Taken Note
In this regard, it is mentioned that HPF and BBUNL have utilized their allocated funds for
VRS during Eleventh Plan. However, BSCL have an unspent balance of Rs. 17.86 lakhs out of their

13
allocated fund of Rs. 13.15 crore. As BSCL has since been transferred to Ministry of Railways,
this fact has been taken up with them for resolution.
Committee’s observation
The Committee notes that it has been for too long that the VRS liabilities are being
settled under lumpsum allocation, is being shown as ‘loan’ to the PSUs. The Committee
would like to know PSUs wise the number of VRS cases settled so far. The Committee may
be informed whether the VRS dues of the employees of BSCL have been settled and what
was the response of the Ministry of Railways and the BSCL regarding continued delay in
settling the VRS dues.
Recommendations/Observations
9. The HEC, has shown excellent results and made good turn around due to leadership
qualities of the person who headed it. It is understood that the HEC sold its surplus assets to the
Government of Jharkhand. However, the HEC has not so far received the payment from the State
Government. It is rather troubling to note that due to non-payment of money by the Jharkhand
Government, the HEC is not able to get the worth of the surplus assets sold to the Jharkhand
Government. It is recommended that the DHI may intervene in this matter to sort the problem out.
(Para 29)
Action Taken Note
The revival package for HEC approved by the Government in September, 2008, included,
inter-alia , transfer of 17 buildings, 1155 residential quarters and 2342 acres of land to the
Government of Jharkhand in lieu of waiver of dues and payment of Rs. 275.51 crore. While the
buildings, residential quarters and 1987.67 acres of land (including 85 acres of appurtenant land to
the buildings) have been transferred to the State Government, the transfer of remaining 354.33
acres of land has not been accepted by the State Government as the same has been found to be
under encroachment. The State Government has released an amount of Rs. 164.21 crore to HEC
and the release of the remaining amount of Rs. 111.30 crore has been linked with the handing over
of the 354.33 acres of land after removal of encroachments. With the part implementation of the
revival package, the performance of HEC has substantially improved and the Company has been
making profits during the last six years but it has not been able to take up the Capax projects
envisaged in the revival package for want of funds. Immediate upgradation of plant and machinery
as well as technology is necessary to ensure optimum capacity utilization of HEC. HEC had filed
an application in the High Court of Jharkhand in PIL No.1783/2011 stating, inter-alia, that removal
of encroachments from 354.33 acres of land earmarked for transfer to the Government of
Jharkhand under the revival package was not possible for the HEC in view of law and order
problems and that the State Government may carry out the eviction after taking over the land and
the High Court directed the State Government and HEC to sit together to settle the issue. HEC is
pursuing the matter with the Government of Jharkhand. DHI has also requested the State
Government to accept transfer of the afore-mentioned 354.33 acres of land without insisting upon
removal of encroachment by HEC and release the withheld amount of Rs. 111.30 crore at the
earliest so that the Company could start the Capax projects without further delay and the revival
process is not hampered.
Committee’s observation
The Committee may be appraised to further development on the issue and also the
possible alternatives in case issue remains unresolved for longer period.

14
Recommendations/Observations
10. The problems faced by CCI appear to be same as that of the HEC. The delay in sale
proceeds of non-operating units and the resultant dry up of funds seem to have held up the
projects of the Company. Similar to HEC, the Committee recommends that Department of Heavy
Industry should immediately initiate measures for appropriate intervention and help the CCI to
secure the funds due to them. (Para 30)
Action Taken Note
Sanctioned Scheme duly approved by the Hon’ble BIFR envisaged the capacity expansion of
25 per cent capacity of Rajban, 100  per cent capacity expansion along with two split Grinding Units
of Bokajan and technical upgradation of Tandur unit partly from funds provided by Government of
India (Rs. 30.67 crores) and partly from sale proceeds of seven non-operating units of CCI but due
to some Court cases by various unions, the sale proceeds of the non-operating units got delayed.
As envisaged in the Sanctioned Scheme, CCI has started implementation of the sanctioned
project schemes by utilising the plan support as well as its own internally generated fund. For
speedy completion of the above sanctioned scheme, sale of seven non-operating units through Asset
Sale Committee (ASC) is in process.
As per the decision of the Assets Sale Committee (ASC) taken in its meeting held on
7.12.2010 to restart the sale process in respect of the closed units through e-auction, tender for
appointment of e-auctioneer was floated on 18.1.2011. It was opened on 28.4.2011 but before the
appointment of e-auctioneer could be finalised, ASC was reconstituted by the BIFR on 19.9.2011.
The reconstituted ASC, at its meeting held on 23.10.2011, decided to float fresh tender for
appointment of e-auctioneer. The e-auctioneer and IT auditor have since been appointed through
tendering process. The ASC had also appointed four valuers, also through tendering process, for
valuation of assets of the closed units. However, the valuation reports submitted by them were not
found in order and therefore, not accepted by the ASC. Therefore, fresh tender for appointment
of the valuers has been issued in May, 2012. After appointment of the valuers, they will be asked
to do the valuation of the assets of the closed units and submit their reports in a time-bound
manner. On the basis of valuation of the assets, reserve prices will be fixed and the sale through
e-auction will be started.
Committee’s observation
The Committee expresses its serious reservation over procedural delay which may
have crippling impact over revival prospects of the PSU. The Committee is of the view of
the revival package should have a time schedule, without which the cost of revival may
escalate due to accumulating liabilities. The Committee would like to know whether the cost
of revival has risen ever since the approval by BIFR? And whether Government’s
component of the revival package has been utilised. If yes, whether the CCI could be
revived efficiently even without ploughing in the sale proceeds of its seven units.
Recommendations/Observations
11. The Committee strongly feels that such waiver of duty on import would harm the domestic
investment and players in this field. The Government has to take this into serious consideration in
the request of domestic manufacturers. (Para 38)
Action Taken Note
The issue of restricting second hand Capital Goods which includes construction and mining

15
equipments has already been taken up by the Department. Machineries like Excavators, Loaders,
Shotcrete machines, mobile concrete pumps are manufactured indigenously though these are
covered under zero duty. The issue concerning waiver of import duty in respect of equipments
manufactured locally is being processed for taking up with the concerned authorities. For skills
development, the Department has initiated steps to set up a Capital Goods Skill Council, with
National Skill Development Corporation, in which FICCI has a role.
Committee’s observation
The Committee would like to be appraised of views of the concerned authorities/
ministries/industry in respect of imposing duty on the import of capital goods including
construction and mining equipments.
