Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee while analysis the working of the Mo U system understood that 
policies followed by the Government impact the performance of CPSEs. For instance, the 
import policy of the Government allows import of ca pital goods and equipment to our 
country in a more liberal manner with hardly any du ty on the imported item. As a result, 
the capacities of the domestic industry which inclu des the PSEs remain underutilized. 
Such policies of the Government adversely affect th e MoU performance of the PSEs. As 
a result, the concerned PSEs get a poor rating for no fault of theirs. Accordingly, the 
Committee recommends that while rating a PSE under a MoU regime the Government 
policy should be included as a measurable parameter . In other words, the Government 
policies must be factored in the process of evaluation of the MoU performance. 
Para No. 35 
Action Taken Replies 
 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) is a negotiated a greement between the 
Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and the G overnment Department/ 
Administrative Ministry to fix the financial and no n-financial targets for next financial 
year and evaluate the same at end of the financial year against the target set, through 
MoU division of DPE as a nodal body.  
 
As per present MoU guidelines, targets fixed should  not be conditional or 
provisional. The CPSE, while proposing targets, tak es into account all concerned factors; 
internal and external. This is negotiated at the le vel of Task Force, where CPSE and 
Administrative Ministry are represented. It is set as potential achievable under the given 
and anticipated circumstances. 
 
During evaluation, for happenings beyond the contro l of the CPSE (force majeure 
type situation), if communicated by CPSEs through i ts administrative ministries to DPE, 
offset may be permitted. Thus, post negotiation, if  Government policies beyond the 
control of CPSEs are affecting MoU performance, the n CPSE through administrative 
ministry can communicate to DPE. The Task Force bas ed on merits can further decide 
whether to accept the contention of CPSE or not. Th is provision takes care of those 
developments which are post negotiation and ensures  that CPSE is not penalised for 
matters beyond their control. 
 
MoU is a tool to measure the performance of the CPS E. The parameters taken in 
MoU are those, which are related to and important i n indicating the performance of 
CPSE. No doubt while fixing the target of a paramet er, all related factors which are 
influencing this parameter are factored in. 
 
Thus, it is clear that the MoU regime provides for factoring in of Government 
policy while setting the target of parameter and at  the time of evaluation. This ensures 
that a CPSE is not unduly penalized or benefited by  the Government Policy. Adding a 
parameter in MoU of a CPSE indicating the impact of  a Government Policy will not add 
value to the MoU regime. 

The parameter based on Government Policy affecting the CPSE will not be 
helpful in performance measurement of CPSE. The imp act of Government Policy is also 
factored in, if applicable at the time of target setting of a CPSE. 
 
Further Recommendations  
 
The Committee reminds the DPE of its guidelines on MoU for years 2006-07, 
2007-08 and 2008-09 which clearly mentions that Governments obligations that have 
a direct bearing on the performance of enterprises and their effect on the 
performance should be quantified. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that 
DPE should consider spelling out the procedure/ mod alities to be followed by the 
CPSEs in the event of introduction of a new policy or change in the existing policy of 
the Government related to them.  
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee while taking note of the mechanism a vailable for revival and 
restructuring of CPSEs in India found that there is  inordinate delay in getting approval 
from the Government which is effecting revival prop osals after receipts of 
recommendations for revival from the BRPSE. In this  regard, the Committee is of the 
firm opinion that this state of affairs defeats the  very purpose of revival. Delayed action 
by the Government exceeding period upto 6 years can  render the financial packages 
redundant. The highly dynamic market environment in  which the CPSEs operate also 
makes delayed revival attempts meaningless. Accordi ngly, the Committee recommends 
that DPE should take initiative to establish an appropriate time line for the Government to 
take action on the revival recommendations of a sick CPSE. 
                                                                  Para No. 42 
Action Taken Replies 
 
 It is the responsibility of the concerned administ rative Ministries/Departments of 
the CPSEs to formulate proposals for revival/ rehab ilitation of sick companies on a case-
to-case basis and refer them to BRPSE through Depar tment of Public Enterprises for its 
recommendations and thereafter for approval of the Government. 
 
 BRPSE has so far given its recommendations for rev ival of 59 CPSEs and closure 
of 3 CPSEs to the Government. Based on the recommen dations of BRPSE, Government 
has so far approved revival of 45 CPSEs and closure  of 2 CPSEs. In case of 2 sick 
CPSEs, namely, Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. and Hindusta n Organic Chemicals Ltd the 
revival plans are under implementation. 
 
 D/o Public Enterprises (DPE) has advised the admin istrative 
ministries/departments from time to time to expedit e action for the revival of sick CPSEs 
in accordance with the recommendations of BRPSE in a given timeframe. DPE has vide 
its O.M. dated 06.07.2005 requested the administrat ive Ministries / Departments to 
process the recommendations of BRPSE and obtain the  approval of the competent 

authority within 8 weeks of the receipt of the reco mmendations of BRPSE. DPE again 
reviewed the procedure to speed-up the revival proc ess and issued guidelines on 
30.09.2011. Accordingly, the Administrative Ministr ies/Departments are required to 
process the recommendations of BRPSE and obtain the  approval of the competent 
authority within a time schedule of 8 weeks as sugg ested by DPE. In case the 
administrative Ministry/ Department fails to do so within the upper time line of 4 months, 
the concerned Ministry/ Department would have to su bmit a Note to the Cabinet/ CCEA, 
citing reasons for delay, and seek extension of time for submission of its proposal. 
Further Recommendations   
 
 No action taken by DPE after the report.

Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry

Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee regrets to note that only 78 CPSEs h ave furnished ACRs till now.

Recommendation/ observation 
 The Public Enterprises Selection Board is part of the Department of Personnel and 
Training. Last year the Committee had observed that  such a scheme came into existence 
when there was no Department of Public Enterprises.  Now, that a full-fledged 
Department of Public Enterprises is there in the Go vernment it is important that the

would like to reiterate the recommendation which it  made last year. The Committee

quickening the process of succession planning in the PSEs. Apart from the PSEs and their 
administrative Ministry, the domain knowledge concerning the functioning of the PSEs is 
with the DPE. It finalizes their MoUs and sets thei r targets both in the financial and non-

 This issue was taken up at highest level in the Mi nistry of HI & PE with the 
highest level in the Government, for consideration of the matter of transfer of Public 

Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) from Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) to 
Department of Public Enterprises (DPE). The matter was duly examined at the highest

 The Committee finds that in the further Action Take n Replies to the 241 
st  
Report of the Committee on Demand for Grants 2012-1 3, it was informed that 
DoPT was working on a proposal to convert the PESB into a statutory body. It was

representation of DPE in the proposed statutory bod y and all existing lacunae 
resulting in problems like delay in filling up of v acancies in CPSEs should be ironed 
out. Also, the Committee expects to be informed of the progress made in this 
direction with in six months. 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee regrets to note that some of largest  CPSEs in India are not 
utilizing the funds earmarked for CSR activities. T his can be viewed as an unhealthy 
trend having a direct bearing on the commitment of the CPSEs towards India’s social and 
environmental wellbeing. It is even more dishearten ing to note that this situation exists

has to take cognizance of this aspect and keep a tab in the future efforts of these CPSEs to 
improve their performance in this area. It is expec ted that the Sustainability Fund would 
evolve as a handy tool in this process.  
                                                                                  Para No. 51 
Action Taken Replies 
 
 The suggestions made by the Committee are well tak en. The responsibility for 
ensuring compliance with DPE Guidelines vests with the Administrative Ministries /

Further, the performance of CPSEs in their CSR and Sustainability work is evaluated

Sustainability’ activities.”

 DPE may provide information on impact of recent Co mpanies Act, on CPSE

Action Taken 
 
 
 NSIC acts as a facilitator for MSMEs and caters to  their diverse requirements 
through its various activities. The major thrust of  its activities is for providing marketing 
support to the MSMEs by way of raw material assistances. The raw material assistance is  
a major area of NSIC's operation wherein major raw material required by such enterprises 
are being provided at the most competitive prices a nd also on time. NSIC enters into 
arrangement with bulk producers directly thereby re moving the layer of middle men like 
distributor and thus supply raw material at the com petitive price to MSMEs. NSIC 
facilitates MSMEs with the availability of raw mate rial on credit and for period of their

has been meeting its funding requirements by raisin g funds through borrowing from 
banks and financial institutions at commercial rate . The fund raised through borrowings

varies from 11.95% p.a. to 12.95% p.a. (simple rate of interest) depending upon the rating

scheme. Total credit support to MSMEs under such ar rangement has been increased from 
Rs.656 crore in 2008-09 to Rs. 3864 crore (pre-audited) in the year 2012-13.

Year No of units Subsidy released

REPORT 
 The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals wit h the Action Taken by the 
Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals an d Fertilizers on the recommendations 
contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred and Forty-  eighth Report on the Capacity 
Addition and Expansion of Manufacturing Facilities of Madras Fertilizers Ltd.  
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Department of Fertilizers, 
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. in respect of the recommendations contained in the 
Report. These have been categorized as follows: 
 
Chapter I -  The recommendations/observations, which have bee n accepted by the 
Ministry. 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its 
recommendations as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
Chapter -II -  The recommendations/observations which the Commi ttee does not desire 
to pursue in view of the Government's replies. 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic 
and explanations advanced by the Ministry and there fore do not want to pursue them for 
the present. 
 
Chapter -III -  The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has 
not accepted replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its reply.

Chapter -IV - The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the 
Ministry have not been received. 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either 
furnished the interim replies or couched its langua ge in vague terms therefore; the 
Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects of 
recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention 
and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER – I 
The Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry 
 
 
 
Nil 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–II 
The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee notes that MFL, which had R&D activit ies in its early years, has 
stopped R&D activities due to consistent losses.  T he fact that Bio fertilizers of MFL 
were developed through in house R&D underlines the importance of R&D.  As the 
company has been making profits since 2009-10, the Committee is of the strong view that 
resumption of R&D activities should be one of the priorities of MFL. 
Para No. 22 
 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
Company has informed that they would examine the fe asibility of restarting R&D 
activities . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–III 
The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not 
accepted the replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its replies. 
 
 
 
Nil 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER – IV 
Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry 
have not been  received 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee notes that MFL was a profitable vent ure until 1996-97, 
barring the year 1993-94.  It is given to understan d that the Company went into the red 
owing to the problems attributed to the capacity en hancement and technology 
upgradation carried out between 1993 and 1998.  Onc e the Company stabilized its 
operations, the introduction of New Pricing Scheme for Urea Price Concession Scheme 
for complex fertilizers are said to have gone again st the interests of the MFL.  Such 
persistent problems led the Company to getting decl ared sick in April 2009.  However, 
the Committee is pleased to see MFL returning to pr ofit from 2009-10 onwards with the 
amendment of NPS-III.  It has been further noted th at a Rehabilitation Scheme, after 
taking into consideration of the inputs from Minist ries concerned, Planning Commission 
and other stakeholders has now been submitted to SB I (Operating Agency).  The 
Committee is also of the considered opinion that si nce MFL is back to making profits 
now through their efforts, it is imperative that th e Government extends a helping hand 
through a favorable approach to the Company.  Accordingly, it strongly recommends that 
the Government should expeditiously finalize the Re habilitation Scheme of MFL.  The 
Committee also expects the Government and MFL to fo cus attention on measures and 
implement them so that MFL is not allowed to slip b ack to become another sick CPSE.  
A resurgent CPSE, especially, one working in the fertilizer sector is of crucial importance 
for agricultural and economic growth of the country .  It is, therefore, necessary to 
encourage and support MFL in every way possible. 
Para No. 10 
Action Taken Reply 
MFL submitted a draft BRPSE proposal for financial restructuring seeing 
following dispensation: 
 
(i)  Write off of 40% of the GoI loan worth Rs. 221.70 Cr as on 31.03.2012 and 
the balance loan of Rs 332.54 Cr to be repaid in 10  annual installments from 
2013; 
(ii)  Waiver of GoI loan interest amounting to Rs. 234.8 5 Cr as on 31.03.2012 
along with penal interest; 
(iii) Continuation of special dispensation in prici ng mechanism under the New 
Pricing Scheme Stage-III (NPS-III) beyond 31.03.201 0 and upto conversion 
to Natural Gas; 
(iv) Continuation of additional subsidy for sourcin g “Nitrogen” through Naphtha 
based Captive Ammonia under NBS upto conversion to Natural Gas;  
(v) Exemption from applicability of Sec 41 (1) & 11 5 (j) of the Income Tax Act 
in respect of waiver granted by Banks/Institutions/ Others under revival 
scheme; 

(vi) Enhancement of retirement age from 58 years to  60 years. 
 
 The rehabilitation proposal of MFL was jointly rev iewed by Secretary 
(Fertilizers) and Secretary (BRPSE) on 4.9.2013 in order to identify a workable solution 
which would ensure long term viability of MFL. Duri ng the meeting it was brought out 
that the existing proposal of waiver of 40% GOI loa n and 100% waiver of interest on 
GOI loan may not be workable option since even thou gh it brings the company out of 
BIFR and the plant is converted to process R-LNG, i t would not be able to compete with 
new plants being set up under New Investment Policy  (NIP-2012) as its specific energy 
consumption would be much high, 7.0 Gcal/MT urea against that of 5.0 Gcal/MT Urea of 
new plants. 
 
 The company was advised to put up the alternate pr oposal of: 
  (a)  Permission to use Naphtha as feedstock till 2016-17 when Ennore 
LNG  Terminal is commissioned  
  (b) Extension of NPS –III benefits till commissio ning of Ennore Terminal  
  (c) 100% waiver of GOI loan, interest and penal i nterest (d) permission to 
invest in new large capacity Brownfield ammonia/ure a complex with the latest 
technology under NIP-2012. 
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee observes that MFL is currently not in  a financial position to 
plan any further capacity addition or expansion sch emes.  But, it remains an indisputable 
fact that the Company could survive the slump in pe rformance in the mid-nineties solely 
due to the Revamp-cum-Modernization and Capacity En hancement of its plants.  
Accordingly, the Committee views that it is extreme ly important to take measures as 
suggested by the rehabilitation study carried out through PDIL in the year 2009.  It would 
help extend the life of plant and equipment for ano ther 15 years.  It is noted that the 
Report of PDIL suggested a capital investment of Rs . 376 crore spread over a period of 5 
years for the said technical measures.  However, it  is given to understand that the revised 
Plan Scheme for MFL envisages only on expenditure o f Rs. 150 crore during the 12 
th  
Plan Period with which the work is being executed.  In this light, it is recommended that 
MFL and the Government should take care that the te chnical measures suggested by the 
rehabilitation study conducted by PDIL in 2009 be e xecuted without fail.  It has to be 
ensured that financial constraints should not be al lowed to stand in the way of it 
implementation.  
Para No. 15 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 Against the capital investment of Rs.376.00 Crore s uggested by PDIL for 
implementing 124 schemes, MFL has already implement ed 66 schemes with an 
investment of Rs. 260.44 Crore that were sanctioned  through Plan funds during 2009-10 
to 2011-12. For the remaining 58 schemes an estimat ed amount of Rs. 150 crore needed 
and the company sought support from Department of F ertilizers for sanctioning of this 
amount through Plan funds. During 2012-13, Planning  Commission allocated an amount 

of Rs. 87.62 crore to MFL and schemes to the tune o f Rs. 87.62 crore were submitted by 
the company. But Ministry of Finance in September 2 012 imposed financial restriction 
on releasing of loan to defaulter companies and ask ed FAs of all Ministries/Departments 
to ensure that further budgetary support to default ers PSUs be considered only under 
Revival/Rehabilitation or any other scheme approved  by Cabinet. Accordingly, no funds 
were released to MFL during 2012-13. Department of Fertilizers in June 2013 also made 
a request to M/o Finance to reconsider the decision  on release of plan funds to the 
company without insisting on repayment of past loan s. However Ministry of Finance 
informed that any further assistance/releases to the PSUs will be considered only as a part 
of the revival package approved by the Cabinet. 
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee understands that conversion of feed stock from Naphtha to 
Natural Gas is inevitability for the long-term sust ainability of Madras Fertilizers Limited.  
It is understood that cost of production of urea fr om Naphtha is very high.  While Rs. 
40,000 is required to produce one tone of urea Rs. 18,000 to Rs.19,000 required to import 
same quantity of urea.  It is in this context that conversion from Naphtha to Gas is 
essential to cut down cost of production and make t he production process more 
environments friendly.  It is understand that the M FL is almost ready for operation by 
using gas.  But it is disturbing to find that thoug h the major components of fuel switch 
over were also incorporated during the capacity enh ancement and technology up 
gradation carried during 1993 to 1998, the switch o ver has not yet materialized.  The 
initial deadline of 2009 has passed without any ach ievement as the Company relied only 
on KG D6 gas for the conversion.  The Company is su pposed to switch over to gas by 
Dec 2013.  However, it would not be possible to do so by this date.  In view of this, the 
Committee recommends that till the company switches  over to gas, it much be supplied 
with Naphtha at the rate at which gas is available.   This will help the company to 
smoothly transit from Naphtha to gas.  Therefore, t he Committee recommends that MFL 
to be proactive in this front and switch over to Na tural Gas as feedstock in the least 
possible time.  It is also recommended that the Gov ernment also has to accord priority to 
MFL in providing access to Natural Gas as the chang eover is critical to the sustainability 
of the Company itself.  The Committee is of the opi nion that the conversion of feed stock 
to Natural Gas is made part of the Rehabilitation Scheme of MFL. 
Para No. 20 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 Company has requested Indian Oil Corporation Limite d (IOCL) and Chennai 
Petroleum Corporation Limited to revisit pricing of  Naphtha, so as, to enable MFL to 
sustain operation with naphtha as feed stock till commissioning of Ennore LNG Terminal 
in 2016-17. MFL has also signed Heads of Agreement with IOCL for supply of Natural 
Gas from its Ennore LNG Terminal, when commissioned  in 2016-17. The company has 
been advised to put up a revised rehabilitation scheme taking into consideration feedstock 
conversion also. 
 
 

Further Recommendation/ observation  
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in the revised 
rehabilitation scheme, as submitted by the Company for the approval of the 
Cabinet.

REPORT 
 
 The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals wit h the Action Taken by the 
Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals an d Fertilizers on the recommendations 
contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred and Forty-  ninth Report on the Revival and 
Restructuring of The Fertilizers and Chemicals Travancore Ltd 
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Department of Fertilizers, 
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers in respect of  the recommendations contained in the 
Report. These have been categorized as follows: 
 
 
Chapter I -  The recommendations/observations which have been  accepted by the 
Ministry. 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its 
recommendations as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
 
Chapter -II -  The recommendations/observations which the Commi ttee does not desire 
to pursue in view of the Government's replies. 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic 
and explanations advanced by the Ministry and there fore do not want to pursue them for 
the present. 
 
 
Chapter -III -  The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has 
not accepted replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its reply. 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the non-i mplementation of 
recommendations contained in Chapter – III and desi res that the Ministry should furnish 
logical explanations thereof. 
 
 
Chapter -IV - The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the 
Ministry have not been received. 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either 
furnished the interim replies or couched its langua ge in vague terms therefore; the 
Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects of 
recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention 
and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
CHAPTER – I 
 
The Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee is happy to note that many measures h ave been taken to address 
the problems including the appointment of a Chairma n cum Managing Director who has 
prepared a practical and hands on plan to revive th e Company and make it financially 
sound and profitable. The Committee strongly recommends that the management must go 
beyond core activity of the Company and consolidate , strengthen and augment its 
subsidiaries, the FACT Design and Engineering Organ ization (FEDO) and FACT 
Engineering Works (FEW) which can fetch profits and  greatly add to its financial health. 
In doing so the Company can be made a vibrant and profitable Company.   
                                                                                                                                  (Para 6) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
In order to strengthen FEDO (FACT Engineering & Des ign Organization), FACT 
is considering re-organization of FEDO for converti ng it in to a separate profit center. 
Further, efforts are on to immediately set up busin ess development offices of FEDO in 
Mumbai & Delhi, which would help FEDO to strengthen  its activities in other places 
also.  Also, discussion is on with cash rich compan ies like ONGC, EIL etc for making 
joint ventures (JVs) for the future projects of FACT, which will help FEDO to fetch more 
works related to Engineering & Consultancy. 
 
 The proposal for converting FEW (FACT Engineering Works) into a separate 
profit centre will be taken up after the FEDO exercise is through. 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee strongly recommends for the revival o f the  Company so that the 
plan envisaged by the new CMD for a turnover of  Rs .7,000 crore and a profit after tax of 
Rs.300 crore by 2020, can be  achieved by raising f ertilizer production to 20 lakh tonnes 
and fertilizer  trading to 10 lakh tonnes.                                                                 
                  (Para 14) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 The revival proposal submitted by the Company has adopted a strategy as under: 
 
a) The improvement of  the  balance  sheet in view  of  the  substantial  
accumulated  losses  and  erosion  of  net worth. 
b) Infusion  of  additional  funds  in order  to  over come  working 
capital  constraints  for  un interrupted  operations 
c) Addressing  policy  anomalies  in  terms  of  higher  input  costs  of  
Naphtha / LNG  by  the  Government. 

d) Taking up various  projects identified  as a  part  of  its  12 th   plan  
for  medium  term  to long term  sustenance  for  w hich  support  of  GoI  is  
requested. 
 
The relief package will bring the company back on t he track of sustained operations 
and help the company generate a reasonable profit.  The package is backed up by both 
medium term and long term plans which aim to put th e company on a path of continual 
improvement in physical and financial performance. 
 
It  can  be  seen  that company  has been  making   losses mainly due to  the  inability  
to  achieve  optimal  production levels  due to  ra w material  shortage,  working capital  
limitations, high interest  burden  and inadequate  naphtha  compensation. Once these 
problems are addressed, drastic improvements in the  financial performance of the 
company are guaranteed. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–II 
The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee recommends that the above stated prob lems must be resolved by 
the Government of India for the purpose of reviving  the Company and making it 
profitable.                                                                                                                  
                    (Para 9) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 The high cost of production is basically due to no n adequate compensation 
provided to the company on account of costly input naphtha, furnace oil and high interest 
burden on loan alongwith working capital shortage.  The Company has taken steps to 
convert its plants for the use of LNG. The hook up for conversion to LNG has been 
completed in the Ammonia plant of FACT and the plan t is under start up  utilizing LNG 
from the Petronet LNG Terminal at Kochi, which is n ow available at a landed price of 
US$ 19.5 per MMBTU. 
 The Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates are common f or all 
complex fertilizers manufacturers, and the selling prices of all similar NPK fertilizers will 
remain almost same due to the effect of market forc es. While declaring the subsidy rates 
for 2012-13, Department of Fertilizers had indicated its intension to mop up subsidy from 
companies having access to cheap natural gas.  Whil e doing so, government is 
considering that the companies who are exposed to h igher cost LNG on account of the 
location disadvantage are compensated by a suitable mechanism.     
 
For working capital and reduction of interest burde n, FACT has submitted a 
proposal for Financial restructuring of company to Department of Fertilizers. The 
Financial relief package sought for the company con sists of write off of the principal of 
the Government of India loans Rs. 282.73 crore and interest Rs. 159.17 crore accrued 
upto 31.3.2013. Besides waiver of loan and interest , company requires fresh infusion of 
fund of Rs. 300 crore as interest free loan repayab le in 10 years with a 2 year 
moratorium. The proposal for financial restructuring of FACT is now under consideration 
of Department of Fertilizers. 
 
The relief package will bring the company back on t he track of sustained 
operations and help the company generate a reasonab le profit.  The package is backed up 
by both medium term and long term plans which aim t o put the company on a path of 
improvement in physical and financial performance. These measures are included in the 
Road map for sustainability.  
 
The scheme for the revival of FACT can be categoriz ed as short term, medium term 
and long term plans. The brief details of these plans are summarized below: 
 

1) Short Term Plan- 
a) Sanctioning of the financial restructuring proposal  to prevent 
erosion of its net worth, reduce interest and ease the working capital strain. 
b) Providing a level playing field for LNG pricing by allocation of 
domestic gas or implementation of a price support mechanism. 
c) Plan fund support for essential renewals, replaceme nts & other 
schemes. 
d) Finalisation of an adequate compensation for Naphth a from 2010, 
which takes into account the increase in the price of Naphtha and furnace oil 
in place of the adhoc compensation already sanctioned. 
 
2) Medium Term Plan-  with a  focus  to ensure availab ility of raw materials and 
removal of imbalances in Intermediates  and  enhanc ing  NP  production  
capacity :- 
 
a)  Revamping the capacity of captive phosphoric acid production 
facility at Cochin division from 360 TPD to 500 TPD.  
b)  Setting up a 2000 TPD Sulphuric acid plant to redu ce imbalance in 
availability of sulphuric acid 
c)  NP expansion at Cochin division 
d)  Setting up a 3000 TPD NP Plant at Udyogamandel to replace the 
two low capacity plants presently in operation. 
e)  Setting up a 2000 TPD sulphuric acid plant at Udyo gamandel 
catering to the requirement of sulphuric acid, oleum and sulphur dioxide in the 
complex. 
 
3) Long term plans-  
 Ammonia-Urea complex at Cochin Division 
 
The combination of the relief package and the measu res highlighted in the Road map 
will ensure that the company will sustain on its ow n without external support and will 
never again tread the path of financial sickness.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–III 
The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not 
accepted the replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its replies. 
 
Nil 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER – IV 
Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry 
have not been  received 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee strongly recommends that necessary s teps must be taken by 
the Government of Kerala to give land to the CWC fo r the construction of the Container 
Freight Station which will help the FACT to restore its financial and commercial viability 
and make it a profit making company.                                                                 
             (Para 11) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
The 25 acres of land identified for establishment o f Container Freight 
Station in association with Central Warehousing Cor poration is a portion 
of the land acquired by the Government of Kerala un der Land Acquisition 
Act and handed over to FACT for its expansion activ ities.  FACT has paid 
compensation as well as enhanced compensation in re spect of this land. 
However, as per the Title Deed/Patta issued by the Government of Kerala, 
this land can be alienated (in this case leasing to  CWC) only with the 
permission of Government of Kerala. 
 
 FACT has approached the Government of Kerala for p ermission to lease 25 acres 
of land to CWC for establishment of Container Freig ht Station. FACT has not received 
the permission from Government of Kerala as request ed. Hence, FACT has decided to 
keep the proposal of CFS with CWC in abeyance. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in case of 
leasing of land to CWC by the Government of Kerala.   
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee recommends that the request of the Co mpany for naphtha subsidy 
may be acceded to.                                                                                                
                  (Para 13) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
FACT is a manufacturer of the complex fertilizer gr ade NP 20:20:0:13 known by 
the trade name Factamfos and Ammonium sulphate. Und er the Nutrient Based Subsidy 
(NBS) scheme, FACT has been receiving a fixed subsi dy as per the annually notified 
rates for the nutrients N, P & S. Under the regime of floating MRP, FACT has been 
fixing the selling prices of its products in unison with other fertilizer manufacturers. 
 

FACT depends on liquid feedstock Naphtha for its pr oduction activities in the 
absence of gas availability in the region. Naphtha is a costly feedstock compared to 
natural gas. 
  
Under the NBS, in addition to the normal subsidy, t he company has been 
receiving an additional adhoc compensation for use of costly Naphtha. This 
compensation was fixed provisionally at Rs 3121 per  MT of NP & Rs 3658 per MT of 
Ammonium sulphate in the year 2010. The price of Naphtha when this compensation was 
fixed was only Rs 36000 per MT. The prices of Naphtha have continuously risen over the 
years and are above Rs 65000 per MT at present. The  finalization of the final rate of 
additional compensation for the period 2009 to 2013 for Naphtha is under process.  
 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in the 
finalization of the final rate for naphtha subsidy.  The Committee may also be 
informed that in view of rise in Naphtha prices, wh ether there is a proposal of 
converting the plants into gas based plants  and if , the prices of gas are likely to 
remain competitive vis- a-vis naphtha.

company to convince the Ministry of Defence regardi ng the relevance and utility of the 
BHEL for the defence sector. It is expected that th e presentation to be made by BHEL 
before the Ministry of Defence, in presence of Hon’ ble Minister of HI & PE would be a 
beginning in this regard. Besides, the BHEL must fu rther expand its activities for 
generating power from renewable sources of energy.  
Para No.37 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 A.  Defence Business  
  The observation / recommendation of the Committee  regarding providing 
impetus for the defence sector business of BHEL are  noted. BHEL will make a 
presentation on its capabilities to MoD as per convenience of Hon’ble Ministers. 
 
B. Renewable Energy  
  BHEL has been making efforts for expanding its ac tivities in the field of 
renewable energy. The Company currently has an inst alled manufacturing capacity of 26 
MW per annum of Solar Photo-voltaic (SPV) modules, including 8 MW per annum of 
solar cells. BHEL has also developed capabilities t o supply complete SPV systems on a 
turnkey basis.  
 
  BHEL is currently executing orders of NTPC Ltd. f or setting up SPV 
based power plants of capacity 10 MW each at Unchah ar and Talcher. In addition, BHEL 
has also setup SPV plants at its various Units, and further, a 5 MW SPV plant is currently 
under installation at the Ranipet Unit of BHEL. 
 
  In respect of wind energy 
, BHEL was earlier engaged in the manufacture 
of 250 kW wind turbines based on design of Nordex, Germany. These were supplied till 
late 1990s, but were discontinued due to drop in de mand. BHEL is currently examining 
the possibility of re-entering the wind energy busi ness with a technology tie-up for a 
suitable higher size and efficient machine. However , the re-entry in the wind energy 

business by BHEL is dependent on the market potenti al and Ministry of New and 
Renewable Energy (MNRE) policy in this regard. As s uch, MNRE has constituted a 
Committee to assess the potential of off-shore wind  energy, and the report of this 
Committee is awaited. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 
The Committee desires to be appraised of the respon se of the Ministry of 
Defence on the capabilities of BHEL in expanding th eir activities to Defence Sector 
and also the opinion and suggestions of Committee s et up by MNRE on the 
potential of BHEL in exploring power from various renewable sources of energy.   
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee views the case of HEC as a classic ex ample of turnaround of a 
CPSE, through a revival package. The progress the H EC has achieved despite obsolete 
technology and machinery inspires confidence that t he PSEs can do much better with up 
gradation of plant and machinery. Accordingly, the Committee is of the firm opinion that 
HEC has earned the right to seek budgetary support and necessary funds for capital 
expenditure without which it would not be possible for the HEC to increase its 
production. The Committee strongly recommends that the Government and the Planning 
Commission must extend all support to the HEC to em erge as a role model in the public 
sector. If the HEC can show impressive results by u sing obsolete technology then it is 
quite sure that it can show much better results by using modern and updated equipments. 
The Committee therefore recommends that the Departm ent of Heavy Industry, Ministry 
of Finance and the Planning Commission should exped ite the requisite approval for 
timely infusing of funds to the HEC. Timely support  to HEC will send a positive 
message to all CPSEs. The HEC, on their part should  be ready with the TEV and DPR at 
the earliest.  
Para No.42 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 Modernization project of HEC partially financed thr ough budgetary support from 
DHI has been envisaged in the 12 th  Five Year Plan. HEC has already appointed a 
consultant for finalization of DPR/ FAR (Financial Appraisal Report) of the project 
which will help in establishing bank ability of the project. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 
The Committee wishes to be kept abreast of the deta ils of the Modernization 
project of HEC. 
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 Having heard the grievances of both the industry an d auto associations, the Committee 
understands that certain problems cut across all se ctors of industry be it in the private or in the 

public sector of the most pressing issues is the lo w duty on imported goods, in adequate R&D, 
import of secondhand Capital Goods, free trade agre ements and skill deficit. The Committee 
recommends that the domestic industry must be prote cted and in this regard the Government can 
take sufficient measures by following the WTO norms . The Committee is also of the firm 
opinion that due consideration should be given to t he suggestions put forth by the Committee of 
Secretaries in its meeting held on 23 rd  May, 2012 for letting NMCC separately examine the 
impact of FTAs on domestic industries and thereafte r to have an inter-ministerial consultations 
on those findings. The Committee, in tune with the industry’s interests, favours non-tariff trade 
barriers and effective implementation of the Scheme  for Modernization of the Capital Goods 
Sector to strengthen the indigenous industry.      
Para No.49 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 WTO bound rate of customs duty for the Capital Good s varies between 25% to 
40% as against the prevailing rate of customs duty of 7.5% which is much lower than the 
WTO bound rate. In order to protect the domestic Ca pital Goods industry, Department 
would like to recommend the higher rate of customs duty of 15% which is still much 
lower than the WTO bound rates. However, as directe d by the Committee the same is 
being taken up with the Ministry of Commerce. 
 
 In the case of second hand import the discussion w ith user Ministries namely 
Ministry of Textiles and Ministry of Road Transport  & Highways is underway and the 
same will be finalized shortly.  
 
 Regarding FTAs and PTAs, the Department supports t he industry against the 
inclusion of machinery for reducing the import duty  further under various FTAs in the 
inter-ministerial meetings held in the Department o f Commerce as the current rate of 
import duty of Capital Goods is as low as 7.5%. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 
The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made subsequent to 
the discussions with Ministries concerned on follow ing the WTO norms and 
restriction on second hand import.

INTRODUCTION 
  
  
 I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliame ntary Standing Committee on 
Industry, having been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred Fifty 
Seventh Report on Action Taken Note furnished by th e Ministry of Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained  in the Committee’s Two Hundred 
and Fiftieth Report on Impact of Foreign Direct Inv estment (FDI) in Multi-brand Retail on 
MSME Sector.  
 
2. I thank the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for furnishing the 
Action Taken Note on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred 
and Fiftieth Report. 
  
3. The Committee in its meeting held on 17 
th  February, 2014 considered and adopted 
the report. 
 
  
 
  
K.C. Tyagi 
                          Chairman                                                                                   
                Department -related Parliamentary  
                                                                                       Standing  Committee   on    Industry  
 
New Delhi 
17 
th  February, 2014 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(ii) 
 
 
 
 

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with  the Action Taken by the 
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in 
the Committee’s Two Hundred and Fiftieth Report on Impact of Foreign Direct Investment 
(FDI) in Multi-brand Retail on MSME Sector  pertaining to Ministry of Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises. 
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises in respect of the recommendation s contained in the Report. These 
have been categorized as follows:  
 
Chapter –I   The recommendations/observations, which have bee n accepted by the 
Ministry. 
 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its 
recommendations as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
Chapter -II   The recommendations/observations which the Commit tee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies. 
 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and 
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore  do not want to pursue them for the 
present. 
 
Chapter -III    The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has 
either not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its reply. 
 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the non-i mplementation of 
recommendations contained in Chapter – III and desi res that the Ministry should furnish 
logical explanations therefor. 
 
Chapter -IV    The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the 
Ministry have not been received. 
 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either 
furnished the interim replies or couched its langua ge in vague terms like noted for 
compliance/guidance, therefore, the Committee desir es that the Ministry should furnish 
Action Taken Notes in respects of recommendations c ategorized in Chapter-IV in detail 
and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 

-2- 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry  
       
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
1. The Committee would like the MSME Ministry to be  more vigilant to see that 
micro enterprises would not be excluded due to cons ervative interpretation of "Small 
Industries" in policy. The Committee also feels that the while focus on "Small Industries" is 
intended to encourage manufacturing sector, local " Small Enterprises" including the local 
service providers like IT service, Transporters, Te chnicians etc. too should get the benefits 
of this Policy.  
 
(Para 26) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
The Government is conscious about the procurement o f manufactured/processed 
products from micro enterprises in addition to thos e of small and medium as is clear from 
the language of the Press Note.  All the above enterprises having a total investment in Plant 
and machinery not exceeding US$2.00 million are eli gible for 30% procurement by the 
above Multi Brand Retail Trades (MBRTs).   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

-3- 
 
CHAPTER-II  
 
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee do es not desire to pursue in 
view of the Government’s replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee while acknowledging the importance of  these issues feels that 
adoption of these systems will increase the costs o f MSME products.  The Committee 
suggests that existing schemes of M/o MS&ME for ski ll training, quality certification, 
packaging must be upgraded and strengthened keeping  in view the emerging requirements 
for mandatory procurement from MSE sector under FDI  retail scheme.  In fact the 
Committee feels that FDI in retail may not benefit the retail sector unless designing, 
packaging, bar coding, skill development, etc., are  improved upon and integrated into 
supply chain.  To achieve these objectives increase d budgetary allocation under the 
appropriate schemes would be required. 
(Para 24) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
To strengthen MSME sector in view of emerging requi rements variety of training 
programmes, including retail management, technical skills etc. are being conducted. A web 
based monitoring system to track training and place ment of trainees on real time basis has 
been put in place.  There is a continuous increase in budgetary allocation for training 
programmes as detailed under: 
2011-12              Rs. 10256 lakh 
2012-13   Rs. 11988 lakh 
2013-14   Rs. 15467 lakh 
 
To sensitize & encourage MSMEs to adopt latest Qual ity Management Standards 
(QMS) & Quality Technology Tools (QTT), Ministry is  undertaking the capacity building 
of manpower in technical institutes like, Polytechn ics & MSMEs through its QMS & QTT 
scheme. 
To encourage ISO certification in MSME sector, the Ministry has budgetary 
provision of Rs. 12 Crore toward reimbursement of e xpenses incurred for acquiring  ISO-
9001/14001/HACCP. In addition, allocation of Rs.108 44 crores in XII Plan, have been 
approved by Planning Commission towards Plan fund o f DC, MSME.  However, actual 
budgetary allocation would be done by Ministry of Finance. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
Initially the game plan of foreign big retail giant s would be to attract the customers 
from the indigenous retail shops by offering low pr ices. In doing so they will completely 
eliminate  our  retailers and  create  a  situation  where  they  will have monopoly over retail 
 

 
-4- 
 
 trade. Later they will sell the same goods at an u nreasonably higher price which the 
consumers would be forced to buy in absence of any other option available to them. Their  
continuing dominance and their direct dealings with  farmers by giving attractive prices in 
the beginning will cripple our Mandis and markets w hich form part of our rural economy. 
Once such Mandis are eliminated the big foreign ret ail giants will manipulate prices and 
our farmers would be forced to sell their products at a low price dictated by them. Our own 
squeezed out retailers and all those associated wit h the markets and retail trade would lose 
their livelihood and become jobless. It will add to  our already existing social and economic 
woes which generates so much unrest and violence.  
 
(Para 44) 
 
Action Taken  
 
 
The Government was well aware of such apprehensions/ concerns. Accordingly, the 
Government has  provided certain safeguards for domestic stakeholders as under: 
 
• FDI up to 51% through government approval mode. 
• Permitted only in cities with a population of more than 10 lakh as per the 2011 Census 
or any other cities as per the decision of the respective State Governments. 
• Minimum investment of US $ 100 million of which at least 50% to be invested in 
backend infrastructure, which would include capital expenditure on the entire spectrum 
of related activities excluding frontend units, land cost and rentals.  
• Mandatory sourcing of a minimum of 30% from Indian small industries with a total 
investment in plant and machinery not exceeding US $ two million.  
• 
Government to have first right of procurement of agricultural products.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
-5- 
 
 
CHAPTER-III 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which th e Committee has either not 
accepted the replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 
Keeping in mind the above observations of the PM’s Task Force the Committee is 
of opinion that the FDI for retail may not have ben eficial impact on the MSME sector.  
However, the Committee suggests that the Government  and more particularly the Ministry 
of MS&ME should commission a survey to assess the b enefits and losses of previous FDI 
policies on the MSME sector to ascertain if FDI pol icy so far has created any back-end 
infrastructure, imparted skills to domestic manpowe r or upgraded managerial skills as has 
been envisaged in the recent policy. 
(Para 11) 
 
Action Taken  
 
The Policy on FDI in retail for Multi-brand Retail Trade (MBRT) has for the first 
time provided limits of investment in backend infra structure which among others may be 
utilized for skill upgradation of  manpower. The FD I in retail has been permitted for the 
first time in September, 2012. Therefore it is in i nfancy stage and empirical data may be 
available after a few years of experience. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The FDI in wholesale trade was first introduced in 1997.  Eversince there have 
been a gradual evolution of the Policy.  The Commit tee had desired that Ministry of 
MS&ME should have commissioned a study on the impac t of FDI so far  on the 
MSME sector, which has been ignored in ATN. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee notes the optimistic estimates given in the study made by Indian 
Council for Research and International Economic Rel ations (ICRIER) on behalf of 
Government. However, the figures on which study is based, need to be validated. The 
Committee finds this arrangement rather strange whe re Government commissions a study 
with an independent research body which in turn dep ends on another non-Government 
source for data and estimates. The Government shoul d ascertain the methodology of study 
and validate the estimates and figures, before taki ng such a major policy decision on the 
basis of this study.  
(Para 19) 

-6- 
Action Taken  
 
The findings of ICRIER were based on the largest ev er survey of unorganized 
retailers, consumers, farmers, intermediaries, manu facturers, and organized retailers. In 
addition, an extensive review of international expe rience, particularly of emerging 
economies of relevance to India, has also been carried out as part of the study. 
 
The Government allowed FDI in MBRT after due consul tations with stakeholders, 
including traders’ associations; consumers’ organiz ations; farmers’ representatives and 
associations; small & medium enterprises’ associati ons and representatives and food 
processing industry representatives. The consultati ons brought out views both for and 
against FDI in multi brand retail trading. However,  the discussions generally indicated 
support for the policy, subject to the introduction  of adequate safeguards. Reports/ studies 
by various agencies were taken into consideration a s part of consultations. Based on the 
studies, as well as the experience of other countri es, it was the Government’s assessment 
that implementation of the policy is likely to attr act great FDI inflows into the country 
thereby providing much needed growth to the economy. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply.  The  Government has not 
conducted any study on the impact of FDI ever since  1997.  No information has been 
given regarding ICRIER survey and the sample base.  Debate in Parliament reflects 
lack of consensus on the impact of FDI in various e merging economies.  The 
Committee interactions with SME associations indicate lack of consensus on the issue.  
It is inaccurate to state that discussions generall y indicate support of FDI.  The 
Government itself should have commissioned a study instead of relying on sundry 
studies on such crucial issues.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
Another significant point is that as per the study estimates majority of jobs will be 
created in front end operations, whereas the Govern ment is emphasizing on the integration 
of small industries in the back-end supply chains. There is no clarity regarding employment 
potential of front end and back end operations. Fro m Policy it appears that 30% sourcing 
will be calculated on the basis of annual front-end  procurement. The Committee notes that 
the Ministry of MSME seeks back-end integration of small industries whereas, studies 
project maximum scope of job creation only in the front-end operations.  
 
(Para 20) 
Action Taken  
 
The FDI policy in retail trading has been formulate d with a view to generating 
employment in India in front end operations as well  as back-end operations. It would 
provide the Small manufacturers necessary scales fo r these entities to expand capacities in 
manufacturing, resulting in creation of more employment in the country and also strengthen  

-7- 
 
the manufacturing base of the country. The sourcing  condition will also enable the small 
enterprises to get integrated with global retail ch ains, thereby enhancing their capacity to 
export products from India. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The assertion is devoid of any conclusive empirica l data which has been raised 
at different forums and by different stakeholders.  Instead of stating generalities the 
Government must conduct survey and generate empiric al data at the initial steps of 
this new policy.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee takes cognizance of several studies d one by industry bodies and 
refers to study note provided by the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP), 
in support of prospective benefits which FDI in mul ti-brand retail may bring. However, the 
Committee suggests that the Ministry of MS&ME and D IPP should have done a study on 
impact of FDI in single brand retail and wholesale sectors in the MSME segment and the 
same could have been factored into the recent policy.  
(Para 22) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
The policy on FDI in MBRT has been formulated taking into consideration views of 
stakeholders including studies done by various agencies. A high level Committee under the 
Chairmanship of Department of Consumer Affairs exam ined the issues/ concerns raised by 
the stakeholders.  The Committee also considered va rious aspects of permitting FDI in 
MBRT. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Committee had sought a study by Ministry of MSM E and DIPP on the 
experience thus far.  The proposed Committee must h ave representatives from 
Ministry of MSME.  A copy of the Report of the Comm ittee under the Chairmanship 
of Department of Consumer Affairs (DCA) may be supp lied for perusal of the 
Committee.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee also takes note of the provision whic h states "in States/Union 
Territories not having cities with population of mo re than ten lakh as per 2011 census, 
retail sales outlets may be set up in the cities of  their choice, preferably the largest city and 
may also cover an area of 10 kms around the municip al/urban agglomeration limits of such 
cities". This provision is open to interpretation. It may allow the mega retail outlets even in 
or around smaller cities which have been consciously excluded in the provision.  
(Para 27) 

 
-8- 
 
Action Taken  
 
This clause pertained only to small States/UTs whic h do not have cities with 
population of ten lakhs. The said clause has subsequently been reviewed as under: 
 
Retail sales outlets may be set up only in cities w ith a population of more than 10 lakh as 
per the 2011 Census or any other cities as per the decision of the respective State 
Governments, and may also cover an area of 10 kms a round the municipal/urban 
agglomeration limits of such cities; retail locatio ns will be restricted to conforming areas 
as per the Master/Zonal Plans of the concerned citi es and provision will be made for 
requisite facilities such as transport connectivity  and parking. The decision on location in 
all cases has now been left to the States. If a Sta te is of the view that it is not in its interest 
to allow a particular location, it is free to take an appropriate decision. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The latest definition effectively nullifies the con dition of minimum 10 lakh 
population of urban agglomeration. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee apprehends that the above provision o f putting an embargo only on 
front end operations and not on back end procuremen ts would enable entry of Foreign 
Direct Investors to all the States of our Union whi ch is not the express intent of the policy. 
The Committee notes that the policy was only an ena bling provision and that it left the 
respective States to take decision for allowing the  FDI in multi-brand retail trade. 
Therefore, there is a need to clarify the issue of back end operations in the policy itself. The 
Committee also feels that such provisions may be mi sused to create internecine 
competition among the inter-State small industries.  
 
(Para 29) 
Action Taken  
 
The investment towards back-end infrastructure can be made across all States 
irrespective of the fact whether FDI in MBRT is all owed in that State or not since such 
investment is in any case permitted under the FDI policy.  
   
The investment made towards processing, manufacturi ng, distribution, design 
improvement, quality control, packaging, logistics,  storage, ware-house, agriculture market 
produce infrastructure which constitutes the backen d would benefit the States in which 
such infrastructure is developed, irrespective of w hether or not they allow the front-end 
retail stores. 
 

-9- 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The response merely reiterates the Committee appre hensions but does not 
address the concerns expressed by the Committee.  
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
In absence of any previous survey on impact of FDI on the SSI sector in the 
country, the Committee feels that the implementatio n of policy provision should be closely 
monitored through an institutional mechanism in the  initial year and must not be left to 
self-certification. The Committee also suggest that  the auditor should specifically certify 
the adherence to the 30% sourcing norm and it must be mentioned in the audited report of 
the Companies which would invest under FDI in retai l scheme. These provisions should be 
provided in the relevant Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) Regulations itself. 
 
(Para 32) 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee took serious note of the apprehension s. The representative of the 
DIPP too agreed to take note of the apprehensions. The Committee recommends that 30% 
sourcing norms should be applicable item-wise. 
(Para 34) 
 
Action Taken on Paras 32 & 34  
 
Certificate issued by District Industries Centre wo uld be adequate authentication to 
confirm status of supplier as ‘small industry’.  
 
A condition has been incorporated in the policy for  FDI in MBRT that, self-
certification will be done by the company, to ensur e compliance of the conditions 
stipulated for FDI in MBRT including sourcing condi tions, which could be cross-checked, 
as and when required. Accordingly, the investors sh all maintain accounts, duly certified by 
statutory auditors. 
 
As regards certifying the adherence to the conditio nalities including sourcing 
norms, it is stated that the approvals issued to th e applicants are subject to compliance of 
certain conditions mentioned therein. Any deviation  from the prescribed conditions would 
result in violation of FDI policy, which would tant amount to violation of FEMA 
Regulations. Any violation of FDI regulations is co vered by the penal provisions of the 
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999. 
 The Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Fi nance) administers FEMA.  
The Reserve Bank of India administers the Regulatio ns issued under FEMA and the 
Directorate of Enforcement, under the Ministry of F inance, is the authority for the 
enforcement of FEMA. The Directorate takes up inves tigation in any contravention of 
FEMA. 

 
-10- 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee is of the view that for FEMA Regulat ion to apply, first 
violation needs to be detected for which an audit i s required.   Self certification may 
not reveal the violation, considering the reported reservations of potential major 
investors against 30% sourcing norms. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee emphasizes the need for setting up an institutional mechanism like 
a Retail Regulatory Authority. 
(Para 39) 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee also takes note of lack of efficient and adequate monitoring 
mechanism to enforce policy provisions and to disco unt violations. In such a scenario, 
leaving adherence of policy provisions solely to self-certification would be self defeating. 
 
(Para 40) 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee finds that there are still some areas , where details need to be 
elaborated and modified in interest of MSMEs.  The Committee finds that notwithstanding 
study reports, a major section of industry associat ions and experts were apprehensive of 
FDI Policy, its provisions and their implementation  in absence of detailed norms and 
monitoring mechanism.  As such, the Committee has s erious reservations over the 
prescribed  Self-certification norms.  The Committe e recommends that auditors must 
specifically certify the adherence of sourcing norm s by the retail companies.  The 
Committee recommends that M/o MSME should conduct r egular survey of MSMEs to 
monitor sickness/takeovers/mergers and other trends. 
(Para 43) 
 
Action Taken on Paras 39, 40 & 43  
 
As per the Cabinet decision dated 14.9.2012, a high -level group to examine various 
issues concerning internal trade and make recommend ations for internal trade reforms, has 
to be constituted under the Minister of Consumer Affairs. 
 
The constitution of abovementioned committee is und er consideration in the D/o 
Consumer Affairs. The proposed Terms of Reference, inter-alia include the following:  
 
(i) to determine the safeguards to be put in place to p rotect the interest of small 
traders vis-à-vis orgainsed retail; 
(ii) to examine the need and the possible mandate for a Regulatory body/ authority 
for the regulation of organized retail trade  

 
-11- 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee apprehends that self certification m ay not reveal the violation 
in absence of audit.  The Committee, therefore, ins ists that the Ministry of MSME 
must be involved in proposed regulatory mechanism a nd that Ministry of MSME 
must conduct surveys and report it to regulatory body.   The Ministry of MSME must 
also discuss the FDI Policy and changes therein in the National MSME Board. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

-12- 
 
CHAPTER-IV  
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which fi nal replies of the Ministry have 
not been received 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee feels that FDI Policy is an extension  of liberal trade policy and that 
the two have hardly any substantial differences. Th e Committee, therefore, does not accept 
the so called nuanced distinction outlined before i t. It is of the view that not enough 
safeguards have been provided for to insulate the SME sector from sudden changes in trade 
policy. In view of this the Committee is quite appr ehensive of the constructive and 
beneficial impact of the FDI policy on the MSME sector. 
(Para 15) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
FDI policy is different from trade policy. The FDI policy on multi-brand retail trade 
provides safeguards for small producers- both farme rs and MSMEs. The requirement of 
strengthening backend infrastructure as well as 30%  sourcing from small industries are 
envisaged to integrate small producers in the value  chain by strengthening their production 
capacities and making them more competitive. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee, therefore, is of the view that an institutional monitoring mechanism 
is essential to remove any unwarranted consequences  of this policy. The Committee 
concurs with the recommendation of the Parliamentar y Committee on Commerce in this 
respect, which suggested that “there is a need for setting up of a Retail Regulatory 
Authority, to look into the problems and act as a w histle blower, in case of anti competitive 
behaviour and abuse of dominance.” 
 
(Para 45) 
Action Taken 
 
 
The Cabinet while approving the policy on FDI in mu lti-brand retail trading sector, 
inter-alia, envisaged action on the part of Departm ent of Consumer Affairs for constitution 
of a high-level group under the Minister of Consumer Affairs. The terms of reference of the 
group include   determination of the safeguards to be put in place to protect the interest of 
small traders vis-à-vis orgainsed retail and need f or a Regulatory body/ authority for the 
regulation of organized retail trade. 
 
 
 
 

-13- 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 
 The Ministry of MS&ME too should be involved in su ch group to suggest 
terms of regulatory body. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee is also cognizant of the recent media  reports suggesting that the 
expected investment in multi-brand retail has not c ome yet and the retails companies are 
negotiating with the Government to dilute sourcing norms. The Committee cautions against 
any such dilutions. Any consultation in respect of FDI and its likely impact on SME sector, 
must mandatorily involve Ministry of MSME. The Comm ittee also recommends that 
National Board on MSME, as statutory advisory body must take up the issue of impact of 
FTAs, Trade Policy and the FDI on MSME sector for i ts study and present its 
recommendations periodically. Any new clarification  on the policy must be discussed in 
the Board. The Committee feels that without efficie nt regulatory frame work, this policy 
will not give intended benefits to the MSME sector, instead it may imperil its very survival. 
 
(Para 46) 
Action Taken  
 
Global investors normally take time to assess a new  policy and its implications in 
the context of a particular market.  
 
Potential investors seek clarifications on various provisions and/ conditionalities in 
the extant policy and also make suggestions. The co ncerns/ suggestions of the potential 
investors are examined in the Department, in consul tation with stakeholders including 
investors, concerned Ministry/ Department, Organisation etc.   
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee reiterates that National Board of MS MEs should monitor the 
impact of FDI in retail and discuss every change in  Government Policy in this regard.   
Board should communicate with proposed regulators, RBI and other bodies.

INTRODUCTION 
  
  
 I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliame ntary Standing Committee on
